atoms.title: Resolve app-contributed inbox sources through the app registry's manifest factory (InboxTypeHandler) + make the PROVIDER_TYPES/handler guard bidirectional
atoms.scope: Provider-seam contract change owned by this plan (the inbox source seam). Closes the declarable-but-unhandled gap for `inbox` and repairs the one-directional #47 guard. Unblocks CE-8 part 1 (Slack inbox source) and EIAT-2 (mail-inbox provider), whose app-side adapters are already written and inert.
atoms.done_when: An app declaring {"type":"inbox","implementation":"mod:factory"} in app.json has its provider resolved and registered at enable-time by a real InboxTypeHandler (registered via register_type_handler("inbox", ...), the same load_factory path every other app provider type uses) and DEREGISTERED on disable/uninstall so no phantom source survives; inbox_providers.get_default_provider(name) resolves app-contributed sources with a documented precedence (app-registry factory -> entry-point group -> native -> filesystem) and its SEAM LIMIT docstring is replaced by the real contract; the class-vs-instance shape mismatch is handled explicitly (entry points yield a CLASS, a manifest factory yields an INSTANCE) rather than by duck-typing at the call site; a fixture app's inbox source is driven end-to-end (declare -> enable -> messages flow through the generic seam -> disable -> source gone); test_provider_types_equal_registered_handlers asserts BOTH directions with an explicit reason-carrying allowlist, and each of the three remaining unhandled types (agent, notification, skills) is resolved per type: given a handler, or removed from PROVIDER_TYPES, or allowlisted with the mechanism that actually serves it named in the reason (skills ship via apps/skill_seed.py, not a provider) — no type is left silently declarable-and-dead
atoms.evidence: InboxTypeHandler graduates `inbox` off EntitySeamHandler's no-op register (which ran the manifest factory then discarded the instance); new inbox_providers/registry.py holds INSTANCES keyed by source_name; get_default_provider precedence app-instance -> entry-point cls() -> native -> filesystem, SEAM LIMIT docstring replaced by the contract; deregister on disable/uninstall proven by an e2e fixture app driven through real app_manager install/enable/disable/uninstall; the #47 guard now reads the BUILT registry (not the single-line regex that under-counted 18 as 14) and asserts BOTH directions, with a synthetic ghost_type test proving the reverse can fail; agent/notification/skills KEPT after a census found native-skills/native-agents/filesystem-inbox declare them. Live, not inert: bundled filesystem-inbox declares type:inbox so the gateway now resolves the app-registered instance.

atoms.title: Similarity edges: write-time kNN over chunk vectors, item-pair rollup, canonical ordering + chunk-pair provenance
atoms.scope: Capability-gap amendment (2026-08-19)
atoms.done_when: an item-similarity edge table exists with UNIQUE(source_item_id,target_item_id), ON DELETE CASCADE on both legs so edge cleanup on item delete is schema-enforced, a similarity score, and the winning source/target chunk indices stored as provenance so an edge can explain itself; after an item's chunks embed, a kNN pass over the existing chunk vector index fetches a multiple of top-K candidates per chunk, filters at a configured cosine floor, collapses chunk pairs to item pairs keeping the MAX (the same roll-up rule the vector arm already uses), truncates to top-K per item and upserts with canonical (min,max) id ordering; recomputing one item must NOT delete an edge another item's pass created — a union or canonical-source-only delete, proven by a test that recomputes A and asserts an edge B-A survives; a GLOBAL per-item degree cap is enforced, not merely a per-pass truncation, so inbound edges cannot accumulate unbounded; the related-items endpoint is served from this table with a real threshold, replacing the unthresholded shared-entity COUNT it uses today; the edge pass runs on the KL-14 maintenance host, never inline on the write path; the cosine floor, top-K and degree cap round-trip through config

atoms.title: Deferred graph-maintenance host: dirty flag + queue-drained/staleness trigger + watermark snapshot
atoms.scope: Capability-gap amendment (2026-08-19)
atoms.done_when: index-affecting writes mark a dirty watermark instead of doing graph work inline; a maintenance task registered on the existing heartbeat cadence is due only when dirty AND (in-flight ingest work is zero OR the dirt is older than a configured max-staleness), so a bulk import coalesces into one pass and a busy pipeline can still never starve maintenance; execute snapshots the watermark BEFORE running and clears only up to that snapshot, so a write landing mid-run stays pending rather than being swallowed; work is claimed in bounded batches with the lock released between sub-batches so UI saves are not stalled; the boot-hook chunk-backfill trigger is deleted in the same change (clean break, no dual path) since a hook that only fires at gateway start never runs again; the memory lint, knowledge consolidation and the graph linker backfill are registered on this host so each runs on a cadence instead of only when a human opens a panel; tests assert a bulk import of N items performs ONE edge pass not N, and that a write during a run is not lost; max-staleness round-trips through config

atoms.title: Embedding batch path: provider batching, bounded retry with backoff, adaptive batch bisection
atoms.scope: Capability-gap amendment (2026-08-19)
atoms.done_when: the ingest and re-embed paths call the embedding provider's batch entry point (already implemented by the shipped model apps and currently unreached from core) instead of one provider call per chunk, and the per-call thread-pool churn is removed; a configured batch size groups chunk texts per call; each call is wrapped in bounded retries with exponential backoff, replacing today's failure-returns-None-and-logs-at-debug path; on a retryable or batch-size-shaped error a batch of more than one splits in half and retries each half recursively until it succeeds or an individual chunk fails, so a provider's undeclared batch ceiling is discovered rather than failing the whole import — this matters precisely because providers are removable app bundles whose limits core cannot know; a fake provider that rejects batches above K proves the bisection converges and that no chunk is silently dropped; batch size and retry budget round-trip through config

atoms.title: Scheduled research reports: source-scope x context-scope x citation-policy, with hardened schedule semantics
atoms.scope: Capability-gap amendment (2026-08-19)
atoms.done_when: a report definition carries a research prompt, a schedule with a timezone, a SOURCE scope (which items count as new material, by tag subtree and time window), a SEPARATE CONTEXT scope (what may be searched while writing) and a CITATION POLICY (cite-source-only vs allow-citing-context) — that triple is what makes a contradiction scan and an open-question tracker expressible as configuration instead of code; each run writes one finding as an ordinary knowledge item so it inherits search, graph and synthesis for free, excluded from the default item list by kind; the agent loop is bounded by an iteration cap and told not to invent citation markers; schedule semantics are hardened against four named failures — an unparseable expression fails CLOSED so a malformed report cannot wedge the runner, a never-run report anchors its first fire on its creation time rather than the epoch, a missed window fires ONCE rather than once per window skipped, and a failed run records its error WITHOUT advancing the last-run timestamp; the due watermark is taken at scope-resolution time, not completion time, so an item captured mid-run is not skipped forever; a manual run is idempotent against an in-flight scheduled fire; an empty scope is a terminal success with no model call and no item written; delivery rides the existing digest and notification path rather than adding a second one

Population measured before enforcing: the only real store available (dev-home) held 1 trigger (`notification-digest`, empty config) → 0 blocked; a 24-config corpus covering every shipped provider blocked 4, of which 3 are credential-exfil/sensitive-path refusals and 1 (`rm -rf /tmp/...`) is a plausible cleanup command already refused at the other two seams AND by the agent's own bash tool (same `BUILTIN_DENIED_COMMAND_PATTERNS`). So this adds no new policy — it removes the one seam that was exempt from the existing one.

atoms.title: Consolidate the fourteen autonomy knobs into one declarative policy (shared with SupervisorPolicy)
atoms.scope: "How much freedom does this work have" is answered in fourteen places with no composition rule: `RunBudget`, `runtime_hints.execution.single_active_feature`, `require_hitl`, `gate_policy`'s risk-scoped auto-approval, the `confirmation` matrix plus per-stage mute, `autonomy.py`'s risk registry / floors / earned trust, `allowed_write_paths`, the `resilience` breaker config, `escalation_cfg.ladder`, loop `trust_ttl_secs`, loop `attended`, `max_cycles`, `idle_secs`, and `SafetyProfile`. You cannot answer what a given run is allowed to do without reading all fourteen. Three independent sources in the loop-engineering literature converge on the same requirement — risk-calibrated autonomy, trust graduated by leverage, and the ruling that the high-leverage decisions never leave — and all three need autonomy readable in ONE place to be tunable at all. The mechanism is already designed: PLATFORM-HARDENING-FLOORS §5's two-level `Ceiling ∩ Profile` with tightest-wins archetype dispatch. Depends on `PP-14` so this and `SupervisorPolicy` are ONE object rather than two competing declarations.
atoms.done_when: One declarative policy composes the fourteen knobs tightest-wins under the `Ceiling ∩ Profile` model, and it is the SAME object `PP-14` declares — a run's supervisor policy and its autonomy ceiling are one declaration, not two. Every existing knob keeps its current effective value for every shipped template and bundled loop kind: a table maps each of the fourteen to its policy field and a test asserts the composed answer equals today's answer for a matrix of runs, so this is a consolidation and not a behaviour change. The path-matcher rule PLATFORM-HARDENING-FLOORS §5 lifted verbatim applies here (never `normpath` a PATTERN — `/a/**/../b` collapses to `/a/b` and silently widens an allow). `AG-11`'s deferred profile/trust behaviours are re-pointed at the consolidated object rather than executed twice.

plans.summary: DURABILITY-AND-SYNC is fully shipped. Sessions 1-2 (inventory, safe snapshots, shard format+validate, scheduled service+retention+drills, backups FE, the inventory-driven merge/restore/export sweep), Session 3 (sync core + git-sync/dir-sync + conflict handling), Session 4 (rsync-sync/s3-sync transports + AES-256-GCM shard encryption + the SYNC egress profile), and Session 5 (workspace time-travel + the §6 portability endpoints and FE) are all DONE. plans.summary: BROWSE-AUTOMATION is PROPOSED with NO execution log — nothing has shipped, so all 9 atoms are todo. The plan builds one app-contributed `browse` action provider for token-frugal autonomous web interaction. It decomposes cleanly along its own session/task IDs: original S1-S4 (extraction → CDP+safety+egress → browse loop+ActionProvider → credential handoff), the 2026-07-26 amendment (A1 folds into extraction, A2 live-mirror+auth_needed, A3 scheduled-actuator), and the 2026-07-29 amendment (B1-B4+VB user-browser target via a loopback extension). Hard cross-plan gates: the whole thing is Wave-2, gated on AUTONOMY-GUARDRAILS (egress chokepoint, safety profiles, budget/model-call chokepoint, needs-input gate, earned-autonomy ladder, fail-closed ApprovalGate) and WORKFLOWS-V2-AUTOMATION-SUBSTRATE (action-node dispatch); the actuator consumes WATCHED-SOURCES' escalation seam; the extension connector consumes COMPANION-APPS' device-session/pairing (§C1/C2 — must not fork it).

atoms.scope: §5 (5.1 two targets, 5.2 corpus+qrels, 5.3 metrics+ablation, 5.4 shared machinery)
atoms.done_when: arm-masked runner reports P@5/R@5 per arm-mask for BOTH knowledge (HybridRetriever FTS5/graph/vector) and memory recall, run separately and read-only, from a personal-scale qrels set mined from surfacing/volunteer events plus a hand-label card; per-arm marginal contribution is a number and a dark-shipped arm gets its offline verdict before enablement; reports land in matrices/ via scorer:qrels

atoms.blocked_reason: PARTIAL — six of seven clauses hold and are SHIPPED on main (evals/retrieval_bench.py, the arms= mask on both retrievers, `personalclaw retrieval-eval`, three /api/evals/retrieval* routes and RetrievalBenchPanel.tsx). Two real gaps closed in PR #2091: the read-only rail guarded only the store the run OPENED, so a knowledge run that wrote to memory.db -- the one write the KNOWLEDGE/MEMORY boundary exists to forbid -- passed; and the qrels provenance was on disk but absent from table.json, the API view and the panel, so P@5/R@5 were published with no statement of which labels produced them. BLOCKED (E6, external): clause 4's source (a) for the knowledge store needs `surfacing_events`, which appears in the entire tree exactly ONCE and only as prose in dashboard/handlers/learning.py -- no table, no schema, no reader, no writer. Mining it means minting LEARN-R4's schema AND its writer inside ES-3, which is LEARNING-FLYWHEEL section 2.5's deliverable. Clears when that lands. OWNER CALL, surfaced not decided (carried from 2026-08-25): RunPin requires a non-empty model_fingerprint, but a retrieval score is a function of the EMBEDDING model -- whether the pin narrows to the embedding binding for this subject is the owner's call. Source (c) stays declined on circularity grounds, and push-context resolver arms have a second blocker beyond the signature mismatch: mem_volunteer_events stores entity_name/arm but never the surface text that triggered the match, so there is no stored input to replay.

atoms.title: Harness ablation runner + skills bench + model-upgrade watchdog
atoms.scope: §3 (3.1 ablation runner, 3.2 model-upgrade watchdog, 3.3 skills/templates impact bench)
atoms.done_when: the periodic ablation runner produces a keep/remove/lighten report for one component per cadence with measured on-vs-off deltas via child-process overlay toggling (live spec/config never mutated), and a no-delta component's report attaches as the ablation-grade evidence on a LEARN-R9 retirement proposal; the §3.3 skills bench replays consulted runs with a skill surfaced-vs-suppressed; the watchdog computes a model fingerprint on active_models.json changes, queues small-budget re-benchmarks, and emits exactly ONE digest notification, with per-fingerprint results.tsv baselines
atoms.blocked_reason: PARTIAL — ~90% was ALREADY on main and well railed: run_cadence has a real call site in durability/service.py's periodic loop gated on evals.enabled; pick_component round-robins with a cursor that advances only after a component ran; the on-vs-off measurement really spawns `python -m personalclaw.evals.child` with the overlay on the env COPY and apply_in_child refusing when PERSONALCLAW_HOME is the real home; live_state_unchanged sha256s config.json, active_models.json, use_case_settings/* and declared spec refs in a finally, WITH a leg proving the guard fires; the skills bench refuses an unverified suppression BEFORE spending a run; and the watchdog emits exactly one digest per rebind. An unmeasured arm was already None, printed n/a, and rendered 'not measured' -- never a zero. GAP FOUND AND CLOSED: evidence_strength was stamped by TEN write sites across TEN modules with ZERO frontend references (measured on main), so the row a human decides a RETIREMENT on read '2 evidence ref(s)' whether the null result was measured on/off or merely co-occurred. Closed as a READER, not a gate: the tier now renders as 'measured on/off' / 'correlated' / 'measured (controlled study)', and an ungraded or unknown tier renders 'ungraded' rather than falling back to a grade. UNMET, and it is an OWNER SCOPE CALL: SEC 3.3's 'replays consulted runs' is PLURAL, but MatrixSpec carries exactly one `subject` and that field's own comment enumerates template id / retrieval-arm set / judge fixture set / use-case -- 'skill' is not in the list. The bench therefore scores the newest harvested case and honestly reports the subject_candidates it did not score. Closing it needs a per-skill MatrixSpec subject form, which is a scope decision this atom did not make. ALSO OPEN (plan-body, recorded 2026-08-23): SEC 3.2 names four watched bindings but eval_judge is not in providers.use_cases.VALID_USE_CASES, so only three are watchable.

atoms.title: Bundled optimize-harness template (budgeted search over PClaw's own artifacts)
atoms.scope: §8 (8.1 the loop, 8.2 stop conditions+budget, 8.3 propose-don't-write, 8.4 experience directory)
atoms.done_when: a starter template in workflows/bundled/ completes a budgeted loop-node search over one PClaw skill/template: candidates are scope-checked by diff (frozen-region touch → scope_violation), scored against the dual gate (harvested-suite threshold AND monotonic best-ever from results.tsv), and halted by hypothesis_abandon_after/no_improvement_halt/budget_usd; the winner arrives as a proposal (template version diff or LEARN-R3 sidecar overlay) the human installs, and nothing live mutates during the search
deps: EXT:WORKFLOWS-V2:v2 node taxonomy (loop node) + allowed_write_paths write-scope + breaker/budget machinery
EXT:WORKFLOWS-V2-LEARNING-FLYWHEEL:LEARN-R16 change manifests + LEARN-R3 sidecar overlays + refiner tool-scoping
atoms.blocked_reason: OWNER RULINGS 2026-08-26 on both open questions; neither needs further owner input. MET as before: the optimize-harness template ships/validates/schedules; a diff touching a frozen region is REFUSED as scope_violation; the dual gate is genuinely dual; all three halts fire; the winner arrives only via refiner_tools.file_template_diff; nothing live mutates. (1) The LEARN-R3 skill-sidecar overlay arm does not exist in the tree. RULED: the criterion's OR is satisfied by the template-diff disjunct as written — do NOT build a second arm to satisfy a disjunction that is already true, and do not re-scope the clause. (2) No results.tsv write, because store.append_result requires a complete RunPin and a caller-supplied scorer has no honest model fingerprint. RULED: do NOT invent a fingerprint. An unscored candidate writes NO results row, and that absence must RENDER as 'unscored' rather than as a missing or zero result — an invented fingerprint would poison every per-fingerprint baseline that reads the same file. REMAINING WORK: make that absence legible at the read surface. Small and local.

atoms.title: Give the unattended-interrupt taxonomy a producer and a reader, delete the member that had no signal, and ratchet both enums
atoms.scope: Architecture: the confirmation matrix + the three interrupts (shipped by WF2UNI-5, which this atom corrects); autonomy.py's "Three interrupts, and only three" module claim
atoms.done_when: should_interrupt has a live production caller (unattended_interrupts, emitted by _autonomy_surface as the plan preview's unattended_interrupts key); UNINFERABLE is produced from the credentials_or_payment registry signal now carried by name on ConfirmationRequest.signals; CONFLICTING is DELETED (no signal a ConfirmationRequest carries says "requirements contradict") and both "only three interrupts" claims are corrected; should_interrupt names every ConfirmationType member and RAISES on an unmapped one; an AST ratchet fails when any Interrupt member has no producer; enum:Interrupt.UNINFERABLE and enum:Interrupt.CONFLICTING both leave inert-surface-baseline.json; enforcement is UNCHANGED and the relaxation this atom refused is recorded as an owner decision
atoms.evidence: FINDING: Interrupt's docstring called its members "the only three things that stop an unattended run" and NOTHING in production consulted any of them. should_interrupt was the only producer, had no caller outside tests, and could only ever return IRREVERSIBLE; UNINFERABLE and CONFLICTING were produced nowhere and inert-surface-baseline.json listed both. Three documented stops, two impossible, one never run. MEASUREMENT FIRST (wiring a guardrail may only ADD stops): the ONLY enforcement seam is gate_policy.decide, called once from controller._apply's WAITING branch. For a trigger-origin (SCHEDULE/EVENT/HOOK/IDLE), non-blocking run: risk safe -> AUTO_APPROVED (proceeds), caution -> AUTO_APPROVED (proceeds), destructive -> ASK (stops), absent/unparseable -> gate_risk defaults to DESTRUCTIVE -> ASK (stops). So today is neither "stop for everything" nor "stop for nothing": an unattended run stops for a DESTRUCTIVE-risk GATE NODE and proceeds through everything else. THE TWO LAYERS NEVER MEET, DELIBERATELY: autonomy.py speaks Mode x ConfirmationType, the engine speaks RiskLevel x OriginKind. autonomy.Mode never reaches the run path at all (run.mode is blocking|background, an unrelated axis). The whole autonomy chain (scan_risk -> type_attention -> compile_require_hitl -> build_confirmations) terminates in _autonomy_surface's plan-preview payload, and require_hitl -- described in-module as "the ONE uniform engine target" -- has no engine reader either (only mcp_workflows:1120 writes it and confirmation.requires_hitl, itself test-only, reads the shape). _autonomy_surface's own docstring states the asymmetry: "the ENGINE's own gate policy still governs what actually runs, so a failure here loses advice, never enforcement." WHAT WAS REFUSED, AND WHY: (1) should_interrupt as a REPLACEMENT for gate_policy.decide is a SEVERE RELAXATION -- gate_risk defaults an undeclared gate to DESTRUCTIVE (ASK) while _classify_node types a gate node as READ/SAFE (kind "gate" matches none of action/transform/stage/infer), so should_interrupt returns False and EVERY UNCLASSIFIED GATE IN AN UNATTENDED RUN WOULD NEWLY AUTO-APPROVE. Not shipped. (2) As an additive veto layered after gate_policy (approve->ask only): safe in direction but INERT BY CONSTRUCTION, since gate nodes classify as READ so the veto never fires -- a live reader of a signal nothing writes. Not shipped. (3) At the action-dispatch seam, stopping unattended runs before OUTWARD actions: this is the one genuine behavioural delta (should_interrupt stops for OUTWARD at CAUTION; gate_policy auto-approves CAUTION). Additive and real, but an E4 OWNER DECISION, not an implementer's: it contradicts this module's own rule that autonomy machinery must not grow a second enforcement path, and it changes unattended semantics for every user template that posts/notifies on a schedule (those runs would newly park for an approval nobody is watching for). Population measured: ZERO of 21 bundled templates use an outward provider (send-message/notify/webhook/call-app-route appear only in bundled/shared/safety-tiers.md prose), so the shipped library is clean, but user templates are not measurable from here. RECORDED, NOT TAKEN. WHAT SHIPPED -- the counterfactual the offer surface was missing: every risk signal caps autonomy at per_stage, so offer_autonomy routinely RECOMMENDS per_stage while still OFFERING unattended, and build_confirmations is computed at the recommended mode. The preview thus listed the stops for a mode the user might not pick and said nothing about the one being offered. unattended_interrupts(confirmations) answers it per confirmation -- which stops survive at unattended, which become journaled assumptions -- and is emitted by _autonomy_surface as unattended_interrupts. Advisory, so it cannot relax anything: it reports on confirmations the plan already raises and changes no verdict. PER-MEMBER: UNINFERABLE KEPT WITH A PRODUCER. The registry already has credentials_or_payment, which IS "a credential"; the obstacle was that _classify_node collapses every DESTRUCTIVE-level signal to the same (DESTRUCTIVE, DESTRUCTIVE) pair, so the request reaching should_interrupt no longer knew which signal fired. Fixed by carrying registry signal NAMES on ConfirmationRequest.signals -- a canonical registry value threaded through, NOT a text scan of the question. LABEL-ONLY AND PROVABLY NON-RELAXING: credentials_or_payment is DESTRUCTIVE-level, so such a request already stopped on risk alone; checking the signal first changes WHICH interrupt is reported, never WHETHER the run stops (pinned by test_uninferable_relabels_a_stop_and_never_relaxes_one, which strips signals and asserts both verdicts stop). CONFLICTING DELETED: nothing a ConfirmationRequest carries expresses "requirements that contradict each other", and manufacturing one by scanning question text is a heuristic, not a signal. The one real contradiction this module detects -- a template autonomy_floor above the risk ceiling, offer_autonomy:404 -- is resolved at PLAN time by letting the floor win and recording it in capped_by, so it never reaches a run to stop it and would be the wrong semantics for an interrupt. Both "only three" claims (module docstring + enum docstring) corrected to two. No on-disk value can exist for the deleted member: Interrupt was never serialized anywhere, having had no producer. RATCHETS (two, because the atom's whole subject is a declared-but-unproducible member): should_interrupt is exhaustive over ConfirmationType with a RAISING tail -- the dangerous default there is `return False`, so a new type falling through the old permissive tail would have been waved through an unattended run; and an AST read asserts every Interrupt member is NAMED in should_interrupt, which is the ratchet that would have caught this finding at birth. Proven to fail: temporarily adding Interrupt.RATCHET_PROOF reds test_every_interrupt_member_is_produced and test_only_two_interrupts_exist (2 failed); reverted by a targeted edit, never git checkout --. The raising tail is asserted directly by test_an_unhandled_confirmation_type_raises_rather_than_proceeding. BASELINE: inert-surface-baseline.json regenerated with scripts/generate_inert_surface_baseline.py -- 148 -> 146 total, enum 21 -> 19, the src/personalclaw/workflows/autonomy.py block removed entirely (both enum:Interrupt.CONFLICTING and enum:Interrupt.UNINFERABLE). No web change: no frontend reads the plan-preview autonomy payload.

atoms.title: Make judge_contract's enforcement claim honest, and rail it against drift
atoms.scope: An HONESTY atom over WF2LOO-1's deliverable, not a feature atom: it makes what judge_contract.py SAYS match what the code DOES, and deliberately builds none of the missing wiring. The module opens by stating 'A PASS without cited proof is invalid ... the verdict is rejected by the contract' as fact; measured, its six enforcement entry points (validate_verdict, meets_ratchet, compute_overall, detect_forbidden_modes, aggregate_samples, hints_from_dict) have ZERO production callers, and the live judge gate asks for EXACTLY ONE word parsed by verify.parse_verdict over a DIFFERENT enum, so no live response can carry proof, scores or a rubric result. Enforcing the headline would invalidate every judge PASS in all 7 shipped judge gates, which is an outage rather than a gate, so the docstring is what changes. No function is deleted; no judge gate becomes stricter; engine.py and verify.py stay byte-identical. Records WF2LOO-13 as the scoped wiring work.
atoms.done_when: judge_contract.py's docstring stops asserting live enforcement and records the measurement instead: six enforcement entry points with zero production callers, both live judge paths named (the one-word GateKind.JUDGE gate read by verify.parse_verdict; the contract-shaped judge STAGE in 6 templates whose output dispatch_infer parses and nothing reads or validates), the rubric's prose-only reachability, and what wiring would take. One rail (test_workflows_judge_contract.py::test_the_unwired_enforcement_claim_matches_the_live_path) fails in BOTH drift directions - enforcement gaining a production caller while the docstring still says it has none, and the live gate leaving its one-word prompt while the docstring still gives that as the reason - with two vacuity floors (entry points must still be defined; the judge branch must be found before concluding anything from the gate's text), proven able to fail by three probes (marker removed; injected validate_verdict caller in verify.py; gate prompt switched to JSON) each reverted by a targeted edit. engine.py and verify.py byte-identical to HEAD, so a user's judge gate behaves exactly as before. WF2LOO-13 recorded with its measured blast radius.
atoms.evidence: FINDING: WF2LOO-1's 'engine tests prove PASS-without-proof invalid' is true only of unit tests against functions with no caller. Live gate prompt: f'{prompt}\n\nRespond with EXACTLY ONE word, one of: PASS, RETRY, ESCALATE, REJECT. No other text.' (engine.py judge branch); live parse verify.py:63 parse_verdict returns a verify.Verdict word only. judge_contract's only importers in src/ are judge_actors.py:26 (Isolation) and judge_pretier.py:246 (FallbackCheck) - TYPES, which enforce nothing - plus two comments (models.py:712, engine.py:1510-1511) recording that engine.py deliberately RESTATES the sampling rule rather than importing aggregate_samples. SECOND FINDING (this atom's real discovery): a live structured judge path DOES exist and already emits the contract shape. The judge STAGE in 6 bundled templates (code-project, design-project, diagnose-run, general-project, goal-pursuit-open-ended, goal-pursuit-verifiable) declares config.schema = {reasoning, verdict, scores, marginal_value, evidence_refs, proof, cannot_judge} and its prompt spells out judge_contract's own five-verdict vocabulary; dispatch_infer parses it (want_json = bool(cfg.get('schema')), engine.py:409). But nothing validates it and nothing reads it: dispatch_infer returns DONE for any parseable JSON whatever the verdict says, and ZERO shipped templates bind nodes.judge.output.* . So enforcement there could not change an outcome (ships inert) and making it decide the node would fail work that passes today - both barred, which makes the docs-honesty option forced, not preferred. THIRD: loop/judge.py is a third live structured judge with its own vocabulary (CycleVerdict{done, done_reason, marginal_value, quality_score, regressed}) and no proof field, so the contract is not expressible there either. RUBRIC REACHABILITY: 6 templates declare runtime_hints.judge.rubric (14 criteria); hints_from_dict is the only parser and has no production caller; WF2LOO-3's claimed 'test asserting every declared criterion reaches a judge' is test_workflows_loop_templates.py::test_every_rubric_criterion_appears_in_a_judge_prompt, which asserts the criterion STRING is a substring of a judge prompt - text inlining, not scoring. No target_score is ever compared to a score. BLAST RADIUS recorded for WF2LOO-13: 7 judge gates in 7 templates (gap-healing, goal-pursuit-open-ended, knowledge-lint, knowledge-synthesis, publish-article, rich-ingest, thesis-tracker) change prompt + parse; 6 templates x 14 rubric criteria become live thresholds; one token per judge answer becomes a JSON object on a gate that runs every loop iteration; the two verdict enums must converge.

atoms.title: Wire the judge contract into the live judge path (blast radius measured by WF2LOO-12)
atoms.scope: The wiring half of what WF2LOO-1 authored and WF2LOO-12 measured as unwired. The live judge path is taught to speak the contract instead of a bare word, and the 6 judge STAGES' already contract-shaped output stops being discarded. The two verdict vocabularies (judge_contract.Verdict PASS/REJECT/REPLAN/ESCALATE/NEEDS_INPUT vs verify.Verdict PASS/RETRY/ESCALATE/REJECT) are reconciled to ONE, not bridged - engine.py currently restates the sampling rule precisely to avoid feeding one vocabulary's values to the other's aggregator. Enforcement lands only after the population is measured: giving a never-run control teeth before the population satisfies it is an outage, which is why WF2LOO-12 deliberately did not. — plus (WF2LOO-15) judge_actors' four unwired functions: check_transition/resolve_transition need an actor on the node-transition path, blind_provenance/assemble_judge_evidence need the message-list evidence the one-word gate does not produce.
atoms.done_when: GateKind.JUDGE asks for the contract JSON instead of one bare word; validate_verdict decides the gate, so a PASS without proof/evidence_refs is rejected rather than accepted; meets_ratchet compares the 14 declared runtime_hints.judge rubric criteria against their target_score for the first time; hints_from_dict becomes the parser of the declarations 6 templates already carry; the 6 judge STAGES' output is validated and bound by the templates that produce it (today zero templates bind nodes.judge.output.*); the two verdict enums are reconciled to one closed set with the loser deleted (clean break), keeping the pre-tier, sampling and cross-model isolation seams WF2LOO-6/WF2LOO-11 built. Gated on a prior measurement of how many real judge responses would satisfy the contract - measured blast radius: 7 judge gates in 7 bundled templates change prompt + parse; 6 templates x 14 rubric criteria become live thresholds (an unscored criterion is a 'not scored' shortfall, i.e. a REJECT, under Ratchet.STRICT); every judge answer grows from ~1 token to a JSON object on a gate that runs every loop iteration, plus a more frequent PROTOCOL failure mode on unparseable JSON. WF2LOO-12's rail is retired in the same change, since the docstring stops saying enforcement is not wired.
atoms.evidence: MEASURED FIRST (the whole risk of this atom): 7 judge GATES across 7 bundled templates (gap-healing, goal-pursuit-open-ended, knowledge-lint, knowledge-synthesis, publish-article, rich-ingest, thesis-tracker) — only 1 (goal-pursuit-open-ended/accept) already asked for the contract object, and the engine then appended 'Respond with EXACTLY ONE word' straight after it, so that gate shipped two contradictory instructions. 6 templates declare runtime_hints.judge carrying 13 rubric criteria (WF2LOO-12's docstring said 14 — one high), and exactly 1 template has BOTH a judge gate and a rubric, so on 6 of 7 gates the ratchet has nothing to compare. ENUM RECONCILIATION: verify.Verdict (PASS/RETRY/ESCALATE/REJECT) DELETED; judge_contract.Verdict survives as the one closed set with RETRY merged in — the loser was chosen by measured usage (judge_contract.Verdict had 0 production references outside its own module, verify.Verdict had 5; but deleting the contract's would have stranded JudgeVerdict/validate_verdict/aggregate_samples or dropped REPLAN+NEEDS_INPUT, and RETRY was the only live member the merge would otherwise have lost). engine._aggregate_gate_verdicts deleted — its two rules (any ESCALATE wins; a split prefers terminal REJECT over spinning RETRY) moved INTO aggregate_samples, which the gate now calls. POSTURE (written into judge_contract.py's docstring, where the code lives): prompt and enforcement are generated from ONE JudgeHints (judge_instruction names the exact score keys meets_ratchet will look up, the proof requirement, the forbidden modes); an undeclared rubric produces no shortfall; score_for matches exact -> normalized -> unique containment so a restated key still scores. Unparseable JSON is FailureClass.PROTOCOL with the raw text on judge_evidence — never a silent pass — and a PASS that scored none of a declared rubric is flagged protocol_error rather than read as 'below target'. judge_actors' four unwired functions closed: check_transition/resolve_transition rule on the gate's actor (JUDGE, or WORKER when self_judge -> redirected to review, realized as park-and-ask); blind_provenance/assemble_judge_evidence build the judge's blinded role-filtered evidence, which is reachable because the controller appends a retry hint to a node's prompt. Judge STAGES: new apply_judge_contract dispatch seam (opt-in judge_contract: true, on all 6) validates and BINDS but does NOT fail the node — those prompts say 'reporting real issues is the normal outcome', so failing on a REJECT would convert normal operation into a failed run. Both WF2LOO-12's and WF2LOO-15's rails INVERTED (not deleted) to assert the new truth, plus PHF-13's audited-call-site test re-verdicted: Verdict.REPLAN and Actor.WORKER left inert-surface-baseline.json (139->137), Ratchet.RELAXED stays inert and the test now pins that split. DEVIATION: done_when 5's binding half is 4 of 6 templates — code-project binds nodes.judge.output.verdict/.shortfalls into handoff, and general-project / goal-pursuit-open-ended / goal-pursuit-verifiable carry the judge's critique into the next iteration via last.output.*; design-project and diagnose-run have NO node after their terminal judge, so their binding is the validated run output. Adding a node to manufacture a binding site would be inventing template structure this atom has no mandate to design. OUT OF SCOPE (recorded, not fixed): JudgeHints.judge_samples/sample_count stay unwired — the contract's default of 3 would have tripled the model spend of all 7 live gates, so the node's config.judge_samples keeps the say; verified_done.py carries a THIRD Actor enum (ENGINE/USER/AGENT over TaskStatus) which this atom does not reconcile; verify.requires_fresh_judge gained its first caller here but judge_session_key still has none.

atoms.title: Make until_dry read the progress_field its templates declare
atoms.scope: An inert-control atom over WF2LOO-3's templates: until_dry termination measured something other than what the templates declare. controller._is_dry(output) returned True only when the output was None or len(output) == 0 and never looked at progress_field, and the output it was handed is the leaf that COMPLETED the iteration - in both declaring templates the judge stage, whose schema carries no progress key and which returns a populated object every time. So for the only two loops that asked for it, the mode's own exit could not fire on either count, and a run burned every iteration up to its cap paying for a model call each time to learn nothing. This atom makes the declared field decide, with one exhaustive per-type rule, and leaves every loop that declares no field byte-for-byte unchanged.
atoms.done_when: controller._advance_loop decides dryness via _iteration_is_dry: a loop declaring progress_field is judged on THAT field (_progress_reading: None/False/0/blank/empty => dry; anything else including a negative number => progress; an unmapped type => unreadable, never swallowed by a default branch), and _progress_value finds it anywhere in the iteration's body - restricted to nodes whose instance for THIS iteration succeeded, since self._outputs is keyed by node id and holds the previous iteration's value for a node that did not run. Body-wide search is required, not preferred: both declaring templates emit the field from the FIRST stage of a sequence body and end the iteration on a judge stage, so a last-leaf-only read ships inert. A loop declaring no field keeps _is_dry's whole-output rule byte-for-byte; a declared field that is absent or of an unreadable type falls back to that rule rather than counting as dryness, because ending a run over a key the body forgot would silently truncate real work. streak semantics untouched (tick.loop_should_continue unchanged). template_lint.py's comment claiming 'progress_field merely names which field it reads' becomes true. Driven through a real controller on the shipped body shape: ends at 2 iterations on two zero-progress cycles; runs to the cap while progress is reported; a productive cycle resets the streak; an absent field runs to the cap. Rail over EVERY bundled template: a declared progress_field must appear in a body node's schema AND be named in that node's prompt. Both halves proven able to fail by probes (call site reverted to _is_dry => the two ending tests red; one template's field renamed => the rail red), each reverted by a targeted edit. CHANGELOG entry under Fixed: this changes when two shipped templates' runs end.
atoms.evidence: FINDING (re-verified on this tree): controller.py _is_dry - docstring 'Did an iteration surface anything new? Feeds until_dry termination' - returned True only for None or len()==0 and contained no reference to progress_field; its ONLY caller is _advance_loop (one call site, so no non-loop behavior could change). The only other progress_field reference in src/ was template_lint.py's TANGLED-loop comment asserting behavior that did not exist. SECOND FINDING (sharper than the first): the output _advance_loop measures is self._outputs[item.node.id] for the leaf that completed the iteration. In both declaring templates the body is sequence[work-stage, judge-stage], so that leaf is the JUDGE, whose schema is {reasoning, verdict, scores, evidence_refs, proof, cannot_judge} - no progress key, and never empty. until_dry was therefore dead for these two templates under the OLD rule as well, not merely mis-scoped: dry_streak could never increment at all. CENSUS of until_dry loops in bundled/: 4 total - audit-sweep sweep_until_dry (streak 2, cap 3, no field), deep-research investigate (streak 2, cap {{inputs.rounds}}, no field), general-project project (streak 2, meaningful_progress boolean, cap 6), goal-pursuit-open-ended work (streak 2, new_findings_count integer, cap 12). Only the latter two change. BODY-EMITS CHECK (constraint: a body that cannot emit its declared field would make the template wrong): both DO - goal-pursuit-open-ended's cycle stage declares schema {summary, key_insight, new_findings_count, evidence} and its prompt says 'Set new_findings_count to the number of genuinely NEW things this cycle established. Zero is a valid and useful answer'; general-project's work stage declares schema {summary, meaningful_progress, evidence}. So no template needed fixing. PROBE 1: call site reverted to _is_dry(output) => test_two_zero_progress_iterations_end_the_loop and test_progress_resets_the_streak both fail (RunStatus.ESCALATED instead of COMPLETE - the loop ran on to the breaker), while the two no-regression tests still pass; reverted by targeted edit. PROBE 2: general-project's progress_field renamed to a typo => the template rail fails naming the loop and the field; reverted by targeted edit, git diff on the template empty. DISCOVERY: WF2LOO-7's status header says todo, but its wiring is present in code and its test file (test_workflows_loop_wiring.py) is where the driven tests for this atom live - header stale, log and code win. No web/ change: until_dry termination has no frontend surface.

atoms.title: judge_actors: separate the enforced invariant from the authored one, and rail the claim
atoms.scope: LOOP-R3 judge integrity — workflows/judge_actors.py's enforcement claim vs its call graph
atoms.done_when: judge_actors' docstring distinguishes the ENFORCED invariant (judge isolation — plan_judge_session/validate_judge_model called from engine.dispatch_gate) from the AUTHORED-but-unwired one (the worker-transition rule: check_transition/resolve_transition have no production caller because node transitions carry no actor — controller.py's actor belongs to the mutation queue), and names blind_provenance/assemble_judge_evidence as unwired for the same reason; tests/test_workflows_judge_actors_claims.py pins the claim to the call graph in BOTH directions and is proven to fail when the marker is removed AND when a caller is wired while the marker stays; WF2LOO-13's scope names all four functions so the unwired judge surface has ONE owner
atoms.evidence: Measured: plan_judge_session 3 live refs and validate_judge_model 4 (enforced, wired at S146 per engine.py:1296's own comment); check_transition, resolve_transition, blind_provenance and assemble_judge_evidence 0 live refs each. controller.py's only `actor` is the mutation queue's (controller.py:1210), so a node transition has no actor to check — which is why the rule was never wired, and why wiring it is WF2LOO-13's work rather than a one-liner.

atoms.title: Reconcile the THIRD verdict vocabulary (loop/judge.CycleVerdict) into the contract
atoms.scope: `WF2LOO-13` reconciled TWO vocabularies (`verify.Verdict` deleted, `judge_contract.Verdict` survived with RETRY merged in). `WF2LOO-12`'s own design already named the third and left it: "loop/judge.py is a third, live, structured judge with its OWN vocabulary — CycleVerdict{done, marginal_value, quality_score, regressed} — and no proof field, so the contract is not expressible there either." That is a recorded gap with no owner. The two dialects are not merely different spellings: the loop side has `marginal_value` (0-5) and `regressed`, which are the product's ONLY diminishing-returns signals, and the contract side has the proof precondition, the rubric ratchet and the actor matrix, which the loop side lacks. Each is missing what the other has, so reconciling is additive in both directions rather than a rename.
atoms.done_when: `judge_contract.Verdict` absorbs what only `CycleVerdict` carried — `marginal_value` and `regressed` become contract fields with the same 0-5 clamp and the same asymmetric adjudication rule (`loop/judge.adjudicate`: a `done` survives only if the skeptic also says done; a `regressed` survives if EITHER judge flags it) — and `CycleVerdict` is DELETED, not bridged. The loop judge's ground-truth observation (`_observe_ground_truth`: runs the verify command, reads the named deliverable across workspace plus fallback dirs, injects it labelled authoritative) survives unchanged as the loop-side evidence source feeding the contract's `evidence_refs`. Population measured before enforcement, per this program's rule: how many real loop verdicts would satisfy `validate_verdict` is counted BEFORE the proof precondition applies to a loop cycle. Blast radius named: every loop kind that writes a verdict, plus `watchdog._publish_cycle_verdict` and the cockpit's ROI rail / verdict panel which read `marginal_value`/`quality_score`/`regressed` off the persisted shape.

atoms.title: Give the loop judge a model binding independent of the worker it grades
atoms.scope: `loop/judge.assess_cycle`'s docstring states an independence property the code does not implement: "in production it resolves the 'reasoning' use-case (a stronger third-party check than the worker's model)". The code returns `resolve_provider_for_use_case("loops")` (`judge.py:218`), and `providers/provider_bridge.py:343` documents `"loops"` as the LOOP WORKER's use case. Same for the skeptic (`judge.py:286`) and for `gates.judge_verdict` (`gates.py:134`). `LoopsConfig` has no judge model field, so there is nothing to bind even if a caller wanted independence. The judge is therefore independent in session and prompt but runs on the same model binding as the work it grades — the "correlated reviewer mistakes" failure mode named in the review-loop literature, and the opposite of the vendor guidance to reserve the strongest model for judgment.
atoms.done_when: A `loops.judge_use_case` config field is wired through all four config points (dataclass + `_meta`, `load()`, `to_dict()`, the `_EDITABLE_CONFIG` PATCH allowlist) defaulting to `reasoning`, and `assess_cycle` / `assess_cycle_skeptic` / `gates.judge_verdict` resolve it instead of `"loops"`. The docstring's claim becomes true rather than being softened. A test asserts the judge's resolved binding differs from the worker's whenever the two use cases resolve to different entries, and a second asserts the degraded path is unchanged (a judge whose provider cannot start still returns None — defer, never a false complete — and still logs WARNING so the degradation stays diagnosable). Cheap by construction: no new mechanism, one field and three call sites.

atoms.title: Give the loops engine a worker-independent progress signal
atoms.scope: `loop/watchdog.check_stagnation` is the loops engine's only progress detector and it reads a field the WORKER writes: `all(int(f.get("new_findings_count", 1) or 0) == 0 for f in recent)`. `agents/defaults.py:89` instructs the agent to emit `new_findings_count`, and `loop/kinds/{goal,research}.py` prompt for it. The default when the key is absent is `1` — "progressing". So a worker reporting any nonzero count is immune to stagnation detection forever, and a worker that omits the field is immune by default. The workflows side has a worker-INDEPENDENT backstop (`resilience.check_breaker`'s byte-identical output hashing, plus `loop_middleware`'s call and fix fingerprints); loops has only `_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_ERRORS = 2` on turn FAILURES and a wall-clock unresponsive deadline, so a confidently-looping worker producing fresh junk trips nothing. `_STAGNATION_WINDOW = 5` is also a module constant while the middleware's equivalent window is configurable.
atoms.done_when: The loops watchdog gains a progress signal the worker cannot author: byte-identical-output detection over the cycle's finding content (the same rule `resilience.check_breaker` already applies, reused rather than reimplemented) and repeated-call fingerprinting where a cycle records tool calls. The self-reported `new_findings_count` is KEPT as a cheap first signal — it is genuinely informative when honest — but it can no longer be the only one, and its absence stops reading as progress. `_STAGNATION_WINDOW` becomes a `LoopsConfig` field wired through all four config points. Verified by a driven loop whose worker reports a nonzero count every cycle while emitting identical content: it now stalls, and the test is proven able to fail by reverting the detector.

atoms.title: Give `on_item_error: collect` an executor + an exhaustiveness ratchet over ItemErrorPolicy
atoms.scope: §2 `foreach` item-error policy (Slice 2c's `on_item_error`, completed)
atoms.done_when: tick.foreach_outcome branches on every ItemErrorPolicy member and RAISES on an unmapped one; `collect` runs every item then fails the container, and its per-item failures land in the ledger as one items_collected record; the three policies produce three DIFFERENT run-level observables for one seeded failing item, driven through the real controller; enum:ItemErrorPolicy.COLLECT leaves inert-surface-baseline.json
atoms.evidence: FINDING: ItemErrorPolicy.COLLECT was a DECLARED STRATEGY WITH NO EXECUTOR, and unlike most inert surfaces it was ADVERTISED — validator.py accepted `on_item_error: collect` and service.capabilities published item_error_policies=[p.value for p in ItemErrorPolicy], the catalog an authoring model reads. tick.py compared against HALT (stop scheduling) and SKIP (tolerate → DEGRADED) only; `collect` fell through to container_outcome, so it silently got a MIXTURE: it did not halt early (like SKIP) but any failure failed the container (like HALT) — neither documented behaviour, and by coincidence the same OUTCOME shape this atom then chose deliberately. What was genuinely missing: a branch naming the member, the failures-as-data half, and a ratchet. SEMANTICS: COLLECT = run every item to terminal (never halt early, like SKIP), then fail the container if any item failed (unlike SKIP's DEGRADED). FAILED not DEGRADED because _ROOT_TO_RUN maps DEGRADED→COMPLETE, so a DEGRADED terminal would make COLLECT's run-level observable identical to SKIP's and the one policy whose point is that failures matter would report success; the branch returns container_outcome rather than a hard-coded FAILED so a CANCELLED/BLOCKED item still reports the more severe verdict off _worst's severity order. ERRORS-AS-DATA: journal, not a container output — no container output surface EXISTS (controller._outputs is keyed by node id and written only where a LEAF completes; the frontier only yields leaves; a container deliberately has no stored instance so a rewind cannot leave a stale verdict), and publishing under the foreach's node id would make {{nodes.<fan>.output}} resolve in memory and resolve to nothing after a restart because rehydration reads inst.output_ref. So one items_collected ledger record per fan-out per epoch carries item_index/item_label/instance_path/node_id/failure_class/cause. FOLLOW-UP (not built): a downstream node is already reachable (a sequence continues past a terminal failed child unless it declares on_error: fail_run), so what is missing is only a way to BIND the set in — either a durable container-output surface (container instance or persisted container-outputs map, written at derivation and restored on rehydrate) or a read-only ledger action provider (cheaper, reuses an existing shape). RATCHET: the decision moved into tick.foreach_outcome, exhaustive over the enum with a raising tail; held by three tests — every member driven, the raise asserted, and an AST read of foreach_outcome asserting it names every member (a behavioural test alone would pass a fallthrough shared by two members). Proven to fail: adding a 4th member RETRY_ALL reds test_every_member_has_a_branch[retry_all] and test_the_source_branches_on_every_member_by_name. BEHAVIOURAL PROOF: one seeded failing item (item 1 of 3 cannot satisfy the body's {{item.v}} binding → a USER-class BindingError, deterministic, zero tokens, not retryable) with max_concurrency: 1 (unbounded, every item is launched before a failure exists to halt on) yields three DIFFERENT observables through the real controller — halt: FAILED with items {0,1} started; skip: COMPLETE with {0,1,2}; collect: FAILED with {0,1,2}. 18 new tests in tests/test_workflows_item_error_policy.py. inert-surface-baseline.json regenerated: 152 → 151 (enum 25 → 24).

atoms.title: Make `on_overlap: queue` queue instead of starting a concurrent run + an exhaustiveness ratchet over OverlapPolicy
atoms.scope: §2 trigger-origin starts (`on_overlap`, owned by the run-workflow provider re-added in Slice 3)
atoms.done_when: overlap.decide branches on every OverlapPolicy member and RAISES on an unmapped one; a `queue` start with a prior in flight PERSISTS an unlaunched run (DRAFT + a marker on run.extra) and returns outcome: "queued" naming it, instead of launching beside the prior; overlap.drain starts it from the controller's terminal write and from the watchdog poll, single-flight and idempotent; a hand-made DRAFT with no marker is never launched; the queue is capped at one and a dropped start names the cap in its outcome and the log; enum:OverlapPolicy.QUEUE leaves inert-surface-baseline.json
atoms.evidence: FINDING: OverlapPolicy.QUEUE did the exact OPPOSITE of its name. run_workflow_provider.py:124-175 compared against SKIP (early return, outcome="skip", nothing starts) and CANCEL_PREVIOUS (store.request_cancel per active prior, then start) and let `queue` match NEITHER branch and fall straight through to store.create + _launch — launching a CONCURRENT run beside the still-running prior, silently. That violates the enum's own docstring (SKIP = "skip"  # default — a per-minute trigger must not stack runs) for the one policy whose name promises ordering: a per-minute trigger with on_overlap: queue against a slow workflow stacked runs unboundedly. Reachable and round-tripped, not theoretical: models.py:730 parses on_overlap from a def (unknown → SKIP), models.py:717 serializes it, native_defs.py:108 accepts it from a def payload, and inert-surface-baseline.json listed enum:OverlapPolicy.QUEUE as inert. SEMANTICS (one line each): SKIP (default) — a prior is in flight ⇒ nothing created, nothing starts. QUEUE — a prior is in flight ⇒ the start is PERSISTED as an unlaunched run and started when that prior ends; ordering, not concurrency. CANCEL_PREVIOUS — cancel the priors, then start now. With a free def all three start immediately (queue is not `always queue`, or a per-hour trigger against a one-minute workflow would never start anything directly). MARKER (queued vs hand-made draft): run.extra["overlap_queued"] plus overlap_queued_at, written in the SAME INSERT as the row (WorkflowRun(extra=...)) so there is no window where the row is a plain DRAFT. `extra` is a persisted TEXT/JSON column (store._JSON_COLUMNS) round-tripped by _row_to_run/_run_to_params, so the marker survives a restart with the row. RunStatus.DRAFT is ALSO where a user's unlaunched editor draft sits, so a drain keyed on "DRAFT for this def" would start work the user never asked for — the worst available outcome of this atom; test_a_hand_made_draft_is_never_launched pins it directly (a marker-less DRAFT for the same def survives both drain call sites still DRAFT with no controller). Rejected: a new RunStatus.QUEUED member (a state-machine change — active_runs, TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES, _ROOT_TO_RUN, materialize's exhaustive state→status table and the FE status union + workflowMeta badge Record all switch on it, and none of them need to; the FE already renders a `Draft` badge, so no web change and no web gate); RunOrigin (it says WHO started a run, not what it waits on); a journal fact (durable but unqueryable — "which drafts are queued" would mean opening every draft's ledger). DRAIN + IDEMPOTENCY: overlap.drain(name, supervisor) reuses concurrency.single_flight — the same flock leases.acquire_claim is built on — rather than a new lock, plus two more guards, cheapest first: (1) the flock, cross-process and also cross-coroutine because flock conflicts across separate open file descriptions in one process; (2) the supervisor's controller registry, since watchdog.launch already returns the EXISTING controller for a run id it holds — which also covers the window before a new controller's tick loop has written RUNNING, when active_runs() still reads empty; (3) an active re-check INSIDE the lock. Two LIVE call sites: controller._finish after the terminal status is written and published (awaited inline — a floating task makes the handoff untestable and can outlive its loop — and fully guarded, because _finish is the single terminal writer WF2-R10 and must not raise), and watchdog._poll_once after adoption via drain_all. CAP: MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH = 1, coalesce-to-one. Depth 1 keeps the promise the name makes (the fire is not dropped, it runs next) while bounding the backlog; unbounded depth means run N+2 does the same work as run N+1 with staler inputs and one late run becomes a multi-hour replay of expired trigger fires. A dropped start is loud in BOTH places: outcome stdout carries dropped/reason="queue_full"/queue_depth/max_queue_depth/queued_run_id AND the provider logs a WARNING (asserted by test_a_dropped_start_is_logged). It stays outcome="skip" (nothing durable was created) rather than minting a fourth vocabulary member. `queued` also gates the immediate start, so a fire arriving in the window between "the prior finished" and "the drain launched it" cannot jump the queue. RESTART: the queue IS re-drained, bounded by POLL_INTERVAL_SECS (5s). A queued start is a durable DRAFT row plus its spec.json, and watchdog._poll_once calls drain_all, so the first poll after the gateway returns drains whatever was pending — no separate boot hook. Driven by test_the_watchdog_poll_drains_after_a_restart with a FRESH WorkflowWatchdog that has never seen the run. Deliberately NOT preserved: if the boot sweep suspended the prior to PAUSED, PAUSED counts as active, so the queued run waits for an explicit Resume rather than overtaking a run that is not finished (test_the_queue_waits_while_the_prior_is_only_paused). A queued run whose spec directory vanished is FAILED rather than left queued — safe for the same reason the watchdog's orphan reaper is safe (a DRAFT run has no controller) — because a queue head the drain can never launch would be re-examined every poll forever and would block every start behind it. NEW OUTCOME MEMBER: outcome="queued". Mandatory ripple, not optional — triggers.executor._record_fire_outcome maps an unrecognized runner status to Outcome.FAILED, so an unmapped "queued" would have recorded a healthy queued fire as a failure and spent autopause's 5-failure budget. Updated in the same change: STATUS_TO_OUTCOME and SCHEDULE_STATUS_TO_OUTCOME / HOOK_STATUS_TO_OUTCOME → Outcome.DEFERRED (its "parked / resource-busy" half) each with their own reason string so the two DEFERRED cases stay distinguishable; hooks.py and dashboard/handlers/triggers.py pass it through instead of folding it into ok/success; engine.dispatch_action maps it to DEGRADED (a DONE node would tell the frontier this action's work completed); action_providers/base.py documents the member and the rule that adding one means updating those maps. "skip" would under-report a real run record and "launched" would claim work that has not begun. RATCHET: overlap.decide(policy, active=, queued=) names every member and its unreachable tail RAISES; the provider call site additionally refuses an OverlapAction it has no branch for BEFORE anything is created, because the dangerous default there is "fall through and launch". Four tests: every member driven, the raise asserted, an AST read of decide asserting it names every member (a behavioural test alone would pass a fallthrough shared by two members — exactly how QUEUE hid), and a source check that every OverlapAction member has a call site. Proven to fail: temporarily adding a fourth member WV14_RATCHET_PROBE reds test_every_member_has_a_branch[wv14_ratchet_probe] and test_the_source_branches_on_every_member_by_name (2 failed, 5 passed); reverted by a targeted edit, never git checkout --. Also proven the atom is a real fix: forcing decide's QUEUE branch back to START reds 12 of 27 tests including the regression test. 27 new tests in tests/test_workflows_overlap_queue.py. inert-surface-baseline.json regenerated with scripts/generate_inert_surface_baseline.py: 151 → 150 total, enum 24 → 23, the single removed line being enum:OverlapPolicy.QUEUE. New module ⇒ docs/architecture/workflows.md module table gained an overlap.py row (test_workflows_hardening's doc-coverage test).

atoms.title: Map every status a fire writes, and an AST rail over the three status→outcome tables
atoms.scope: §7 criterion 4 (one run-history feed, typed outcomes) + criterion 8 (zero silent drops)
atoms.done_when: HOOK_STATUS_TO_OUTCOME names launched + skipped_incident and SCHEDULE_STATUS_TO_OUTCOME names blocked_injection + all six INERT_OUTCOMES, so no live status reaches a .get() fallback; both fallbacks LOG the status they could not classify and never return ran; a suppressed or screened row is LEDGER weight and lands in feed_response's suppressed half; tests/test_triggers_status_vocabulary.py infers each writer's possible values from its own AST (conditional expressions, in/not in guards, local names) with per-writer vacuity floors and a pinned writer-file census, and reds on all nine statuses if the tables are reverted
atoms.evidence: FINDING: a projection table is only as honest as the writers it was authored against. triggers/history.py translates each store's status word into a FIRE_OUTCOMES member and reads its table with .get(status, <fallback>). WV-14 updated all three tables for the NEW member (queued) because a new member's ripple is obvious; the statuses already being written when the tables were authored are the ones nobody re-checked, and NINE values across FOUR writers were live and unmapped. hooks.py:590 writes skipped_incident (incident kill switch, returns BEFORE the provider is called) and hooks.py:653 writes launched — both fell to hook_to_record's `RAN if last_run`, i.e. "it ran and did something durable" for a hook that ran nothing. gateway.py:1429 (_record_blocked_fire) writes status="blocked_injection" and service.py:665 (_record_suppression_row) writes all six INERT_OUTCOMES members into ScheduleRun.status — both fell to schedule_run_to_record's FAILED, so a DEFENDED injection attempt and a quiet-hours skip both read as genuine failures, and the suppression rows also stayed in feed_response's `did` half instead of folding into `suppressed_ids`, burying the fires that mattered. THE SILENT FALLBACK IS THE DEFECT, not the missing key: both fallbacks were individually defensible (RAN-if-last-run = "we know it ran, we lack the verdict"; FAILED = FireRecord.from_dict's "unclassifiable must not count as a success") and neither said anything, which is how four statuses survived two sessions that edited these very tables. MAPPINGS (each with its reason in a code comment, and what a user now sees): launched → DEFERRED in the hook table, matching SCHEDULE_STATUS_TO_OUTCOME and executor.STATUS_TO_OUTCOME (T7: started ≠ succeeded; the background turn records its own outcome in its own run) — the user sees an info-toned "deferred" with "outcome not yet known" instead of a green tick. skipped_incident → SKIPPED_GATE: nothing ran, nothing was spent, nothing changed, which is SKIPPED_GATE's family (quiet-hours / cooldown / condition-false) and, via INERT_OUTCOMES, a ledger row that folds out of the default runs inbox — NOT REFUSED (blocked already carries that: a denylist refusal is a verdict on THIS action, while an incident suspends every automated action and lifts on its own) and NOT DEFERRED (deferred work still starts; this fire is dropped and never retried) — the user sees a neutral grey suppression naming the incident, in the archived half, instead of "ran". blocked_injection → BLOCKED_INJECTION, the member that exists for exactly this row: the user sees the red-shield "blocked" badge statusMeta already renders instead of "failed", and the row leaves TRUE_FAILURE_OUTCOMES so a defence stops looking like a fault. The six INERT_OUTCOMES → themselves, identity BY CONSTRUCTION (**{v: v for v in sorted(INERT_OUTCOMES)}) rather than six hand-copied lines, because the writer's own guard is `outcome not in INERT_OUTCOMES: return` — that set IS the vocabulary and a seventh member needs no second edit; the user sees each suppression as the suppression it was, in suppressed_ids, with the reason _record_suppression_row already stored. NO NEW VOCABULARY MEMBER, deliberately: all nine landed on existing Outcome members. WV-14 paid that cost (three tables + engine.dispatch_action + the FE union) and nothing here needed it. weight moved instead: LEDGER_WEIGHT_OUTCOMES (deferred ∪ blocked_injection ∪ inert) replaces the hook projection's hardcoded FULL and the schedule projection's DEFERRED-only check, since FULL means "earned a run directory and a journal" and a fire that never reached a runner has no exit code to show. FALLBACKS ARE NOW LOUD: schedule_run_to_record warns on any non-empty unmapped status, and hook_to_record splits into three explicit cases — mapped; absent ("", a store row written before the field existed, the one case that still reads RAN because "it ran" is the fact we have and the verdict is what is missing, and it cannot hide a new status since an executing hook always writes one of the literals); unmapped-and-loud (FAILED + a warning naming it). AUTOPAUSE IS UNTOUCHED, and that is itself a finding: autopause.consecutive_failures_from reads the RAW store rows (trigger → outcome → status) and already skips inert exit types, so the mis-projection never spent the failure budget — it was purely a history/UI lie and the fix moves no autopause decision. RAIL (tests/test_triggers_status_vocabulary.py, new): AST-based because a regex finds only the easy half — the owner's own grep over hooks.py found skipped_incident and MISSED launched, whose write is `hook.last_status = result.outcome if result.outcome in ("launched", "queued") else "ok"`, a NAME whose values live in the condition's `in` tuple. Two of the four writers have that shape, service.py writes a variable pinned by an early-return `not in` guard, and the manual-fire handler writes a local assigned in four branches then passed as `status=status`. So the rail infers each write's POSSIBLE VALUES: constants, both arms of an IfExp, str()/`or` unwrapping, local-name resolution, and in/not-in guards — GUARDS FIRST, because `status=outcome` resolves to {""} through its assignment and to the correct six through its guard. The boolean handling is asymmetric on purpose: `A and B` holding implies B, and `not (A or B)` implies `not B`; nothing else proves anything about one operand, so nothing else is guessed (an unreadable comparator pins NOTHING rather than guessing). Anything unresolvable FAILS rather than counting as clean. VACUITY + THE SECOND DRIFT DIRECTION: per-writer min_sites/min_values floors measured against the real source (hooks 8/7, gateway-ScheduleRun 2/3, service 1/6, manual-fire 1/4, gateway-_runner 2/2), and test_the_writer_file_census_is_pinned enumerates every module that assigns .last_status or constructs a ScheduleRun — a NEW writer file is drift no per-file scan can see. web_poll.py is named in that census as writing an int HTTP status to a different entity, so its absence from the tables is a decision on the record. atoms.title: Stop the suite writing to the developer's real ~/.personalclaw, and add the rail that fails when it does
atoms.scope: Reopens the CRE-6 test-isolation strand: CRE-6 fixed cross-test bleed but a run with no home patch still bound the REAL home. Fixes the two seams every writer reaches the real home through (test-side), converts the three module-level constants that froze a home at import time to call-time resolvers (src-side, the one shape no fixture can reach), and adds the session-scoped detector that fails the run on the next leak.
atoms.done_when: An UNSPECIFIED home resolves to a per-test tmp dir at both seams that reach the real one (config.loader.config_dir, including every module-level binding of that function object, and sel._default_dir), while an EXPLICIT $PERSONALCLAW_HOME — including one pointed deliberately at the real home — and a repointed $HOME/Path.home both pass through untouched, so the real-home refusal rails (test_seed main-home with and without --seed-replace, test_cli_gateway_flags yolo) stay non-vacuous; the three module-level constants that froze a home at IMPORT time — the one shape no fixture can reach — are converted to call-time resolvers in src/ (subagent_persistence._subagents_dir, session_map._sessions_dir, and a dead schedule._DEFAULT_DIR whose import-time config_dir() mkdir'd the real home merely by importing the module), with the two tests that monkeypatched the constant realigned to the new seam rather than weakened; the measured leaks read 0 bytes after the fix (-k "project or memory or knowledge or recall" 44,402 -> 0; test_learning_routes 8,961 -> 0; full suite 26 real-home families / 123 deletions / -151,963 audit-log bytes -> 0), confirmed by BOTH the rail and an independent snapshot diff; a session-scoped rail walks the real home once at pytest_sessionfinish (controller only), NAMES every entry created/modified/grown/deleted during the run and FAILS the session; ALLOWED_RESIDUE is empty and exact-match only (no prefix/glob baseline); an absent real home is reported as "nothing to compare" rather than converted into a failure; and the detector is importable and proven to fire against a fake root under tmp_path (append, create, byte-identical rewrite, deletion-via-parent, symlink non-follow, no-write-during-scan) rather than by writing to the real home to prove a point
atoms.evidence: Root cause was one line per seam: sel.py's `self._dir = base_dir or _default_dir()` (CRE-6's _reset_sel_singleton gives every test a FRESH SEL, and a fresh SEL with no home patch binds the REAL home) plus config_dir()'s Path.home() fallback behind 153 call sites. Writers attributed by instrumenting open/os.open/os.mkdir/os.replace/sqlite3.connect/Path.write_* rather than by reading code — that is what showed 26 families reducing to 2 seams. Fixed test-side in conftest._isolate_real_home_writers (declared ABOVE _reset_sel_singleton so it tears down last, or the next sel() construction re-leaks); a global PERSONALCLAW_HOME (removed by CRE-6) and a blanket Path.home patch (rejected in _isolate_session_map, and it would also redefine the Path.home()/.aws and /.ssh paths the sensitivity tests assert on) were both re-rejected in the docstring. Rail has teeth because the post-fix population is zero, not because zero was assumed. The rail then EARNED its keep on its first full run: 147 entries still landed in subagents/ because subagent_persistence froze `config_dir() / "subagents"` at module scope, which no fixture can reach and which also made production ignore a $PERSONALCLAW_HOME set after first import — fixed at source, class swept (session_map._SESSIONS_DIR was worse: its readers decide whether a session EXISTS, so prune() consulted the developer's real sessions/). Post-fix residue is zero, confirmed by the rail AND an out-of-band size+mtime snapshot diff, so ALLOWED_RESIDUE stays empty.

atoms.title: §3.3 cursor rule call site: the spool drain acts on drain_decision instead of acking unconditionally
atoms.scope: §3.3 consumer cursor rule ("the trigger-spool.jsonl drain adopts this rule"); §3.2 peek-then-deliver-then-ack; §7 crit 7 (no double-fire / no lost fire) and crit 8 (no silent drop); triggers/dispatch.py + triggers/loop.py
atoms.done_when: the spool drain classifies each re-entry into Handling at an explicit side-effect boundary, calls drain_decision, and acts on every DrainAction (consume/hold/give-up/skip-duplicate) with a durable retry budget; a failure AFTER the boundary is never retried; SKIP_CYCLE deleted for want of an honest producer; exhaustiveness ratchet over both enums with a raising tail
atoms.evidence: THE FINDING: dispatch.py shipped a complete, documented, unit-tested decision layer for the event drain with ZERO production callers -- `grep -rn 'Handling\.' src/` outside its own definition returned nothing, and `drain_decision(` matched the definition plus tests only. The real drain (loop.py::_drain_spool) re-entered each spooled envelope through emit_event, caught everything with a logger.warning, and did `handled += 1` UNCONDITIONALLY; its own comment said holding 'would retry it on every tick forever -- the poison pill `drain_decision` names', naming the function it never called. So the retry/hold policy, the bounded budget and the poison-pill give-up were all inert and a transient re-entry failure was swallowed as a delivered fire. SIDE-EFFECT BOUNDARY = the `emit_event(...)` call itself, enforced by two separate try blocks in the new `_reenter_spooled`: above it the drain only reads the envelope, builds kwargs and resolves `get_engine()` (side-effect-free, and resolved LAST on purpose -- emit_event swallows an unreachable engine into a logger.debug, so asking above the line turns a silent loss of the whole batch into a bounded retry); below it the envelope is DELIVERED whatever happens, because the drain cannot know how far emit_event got and 'I don't know' must not become a retry. Pinned by test_a_failure_AFTER_the_side_effect_boundary_is_NEVER_retried, which makes emit_event raise AFTER recording that it was entered and asserts the spool is acked, the hold sidecar empty, and a second tick does not re-enter. DEPS: WF2AUT-1 owns the §3.3 delivery contract that DECLARES Handling/DrainAction/drain_decision (dispatch.py, S64); WF2AUT-2 owns the tick loop that contains the drain and the 'no double/lost fire' criterion this must not regress (loop.py, S100/S142). Both done; nothing else in the plan touches the spool. DURABLE BUDGET: held_retries lives in a one-record sidecar `trigger-spool-hold.json` keyed on the DETERMINISTIC event_id (not Cursor.seq -- every spooled envelope is written seq=0 by event_triggers._spool). One record suffices because HOLD is head-of-line, which also makes the file self-pruning; a sidecar rather than a field on the spooled line because trigger-spool.jsonl is append-only and rewriting a line would have to re-serialize lines a concurrent spool_fire may have appended, trading a bounded retry for a lost fire. write_spool_hold returns whether it persisted and the drain HONOURS it: an unbudgetable hold is acked loudly, since an unbounded retry across restarts is worse than the ack it replaced. CLEAR_SPOOL: it can express a PREFIX ack only (`lines[handled:]`), so HOLD is necessarily head-of-line -- ack the consumed prefix, stop at the first envelope to hold, leave it plus the tail on disk in order. An arbitrary keep-set was rejected for the concurrent-append reason above; blocking is bounded by MAX_TRANSIENT_RETRIES ticks and the transient this exists for fails the whole batch identically. PER MEMBER: SKIP_DUPLICATE WIRED (producer = the shipped is_duplicate over the deterministic payload_hash inside DEDUP_WINDOW_SECS, compared on EMIT times so a family an hour apart stays two facts); SKIP_CYCLE DELETED -- a cycle skip needs a trigger_id to compare Envelope.spawned_by against and the drain has none (it re-enters through emit_event, which matches every stored trigger), and nothing in production writes spawned_by at all (measured: zero writers outside dispatch.py). Handling.PERMANENT also gained an honest producer and it fixed a real drop: an envelope with no event kind used to reach emit_event with an empty event_type, match nothing, and be counted as a delivered fire. drain_decision's transient rules were the FALLTHROUGH, so an unknown handling string inherited 'retry five times then drop' -- now an explicit TRANSIENT branch plus a raising tail. RATCHET (the WV-13/WV-14 pattern): AST over _drain_spool's source must name every DrainAction member and over drain_decision's source every Handling member (both measured exact: 4/4 and 3/3), both functions carry a raising tail proven reachable by a test, and every Handling member is proven PRODUCED at the real boundary rather than merely branched. All 9 behavioural tests drive tick_once, never drain_decision directly. GATE: make lint clean (black/isort/flake8/mypy 804 files); 1966 passed / 2 skipped on -k 'dispatch or trigger or spool or drain'; inert-surface-baseline.json regenerated -- a SHRINK (dispatch.py entry removed entirely, enum 23->21, total 150->148).
