atoms.title: Carry a source-declared item kind through to the inbox row (core)
atoms.scope: Follow-on to EIAT-1/EIAT-2, core only — the missing half of the source→inbox seam: IncomingMessage.kind plus its validated resolution into InboxItem.item_kind. The app-side writers (mail-inbox → email, a channel source → mention) are apps-repo work and out of scope.
atoms.done_when: A source declaring kind="email" (or "mention") produces a row whose PERSISTED item_kind is that kind, selected by GET /api/inbox?kind=email, counted in GET /api/inbox/kinds, and equal to the value the dashboard's kind filter compares — proven by a round trip driven from the filesystem source's own inbox/incoming/ directory through poll → ingest → disk → API, not by a dataclass unit test; a kind outside the channel-shaped set (including core's own non-channel attention kinds) is REFUSED with a warning naming the source and the rejected value while the row still arrives as message (never silently, never dropped); SOURCE_DECLARABLE_KINDS is asserted equal to ItemKind minus NON_CHANNEL_KINDS so a future enum member cannot skip the decision, and every declarable kind has a frontend chip (parity test against inboxMeta.ts); inert-surface-baseline.json regenerated on the shrink (enum:ItemKind.EMAIL + enum:ItemKind.MENTION cleared, 154 → 152); make lint + targeted pytest + make test green.
atoms.evidence: The inbox shipped LIVE READERS for two kinds nothing could write: inboxMeta.ts declares mention/email chips, InboxPage filters (it.item_kind || 'message') === kind, handlers_inbox filters ?kind= and counts /api/inbox/kinds, inbox.py persists item_kind — but IncomingMessage had NO kind field, so _ingest built every polled row with the dataclass default and ItemKind.EMAIL/MENTION were unreachable by construction (both censused inert in inert-surface-baseline.json). Fix: IncomingMessage.kind (default message) → _resolve_source_kind() → InboxItem.item_kind, with SOURCE_DECLARABLE_KINDS = ItemKind minus NON_CHANNEL_KINDS (message/mention/email) as the one validation point for every present and future source. Unknown-kind posture: refuse the CLAIM, keep the MESSAGE, warn naming the source and the value — trusting it would let a source mint a kind no chip can render or claim a non-channel attention kind (a row with no refs/deep-link/reply), while dropping the message would let one typo ("mail") silently stop a user's mail and wedge the filesystem poll batch on that file forever. Core NEVER infers a kind: no text scan for the operator's name (evaluate_alert does that for alerting, a soft signal, not a durable classification). Live core writer: filesystem_source passes the batch entry's declared kind through, so both email and mention are reachable and proven end-to-end — as declared kinds, not core-derived ones. The native push source was left alone deliberately: relabelling agent-posted items would move them into NON_CHANNEL_KINDS and kill the can_reply reply-routing native questions depend on. ItemStatus.SENT untouched (EIAT-3's reply path, owner-gated on draft-by-default). Tests: tests/test_inbox_item_kind_seam.py — real round trip (batch dropped in <home>/inbox/incoming/ → FilesystemSourceProvider.poll → _poll_once → fresh store re-read from disk → api_inbox_list/api_inbox_kinds), refusal cases with the warning asserted, the ItemKind-minus-NON_CHANNEL_KINDS ratchet, and an inboxMeta.ts chip-parity test (the reader half). inert-surface-baseline regenerated with its own generator on the legitimate shrink: src/personalclaw/inbox.py 3→1, totals 154→152, enum 27→25. No FE change needed (the InboxItemKind union and ITEM_KINDS were already exhaustive; chips are built from what's present, so they light up the moment a row lands). No SDK export added — it would have been a new inert sdk_export surface. Apps-repo follow-on: mail-inbox passes kind="email"; a channel source passes kind="mention" when the vendor payload lists the operator among a message's at-mention ids.

atoms.blocked_reason: PARTIAL — the NUMBERS half is fully SHIPPED on main and railed: _turn_complete_line carries cache_read_tokens / cache_creation_tokens / cache_hit_pct / cache_saved_usd from a live call site; stats.cache_hit_pct returns an honest None on a zero denominator; pricing.cache_savings_usd computes both sides THROUGH estimate_cost so the rate lookup cannot drift, returns None (never 0.0) for an unpriced model, and leaves a negative saving unclamped. 'No second store' holds structurally and is AST-enforced. UNMET is the V2 live-run half, and it is environment-gated not code-gated: (a) no Bedrock inference-profile id resolves to a price row, so a real run renders 'saved unpriced' -- fixing that is _rates id normalisation, a repo-wide pricing change; (b) no OPENAI_API_KEY here, and it is coupled to PCS-3's still-unmet clause that the OpenAI adapter declare AUTOMATIC (today llm/openai.py declares no posture and inherits PromptCache.NONE). SEPARATELY: the FRONTEND reader is unrailed -- ChatPage folds activityKind==='stats' and gates its rendering, but no FE test covers that kind, so the production reader of these numbers could be deleted with every gate green. Left alone deliberately: the atom's own dep row assigns the readout to EXT:COST-AND-TOKEN-OBSERVABILITY. OWNER CALL: three independent audit passes now recommend SPLITTING this atom -- the numbers half has no remaining work or risk, and the live-provider half cannot be closed from this environment at all.

atoms.title: Discord channel app (Gateway WS + REST over httpx): gateway client, delivery+buttons, transport+trust, setup/doctor
atoms.scope: Sessions 4-5 — Discord: T4.1–T4.4 + V4; Design §S4-5; Contracts C3 (Discord column)
atoms.done_when: fake-WS tests cover identify/heartbeat/ack/resume/dispatch (guilds, guild_messages, direct_messages, message_content intents); REST delivery tests incl. 429-bucket backoff and approval-button round-trip; transport passes trust integration (DM pairing, guild channels tracked-only, fencing) with honest capabilities; setup/doctor configure end to end; V4 real-test-server validation recorded (owner task 3: Discord app+bot+server)
atoms.evidence: PersonalClawApps/discord-channel/ — ChannelTransportProvider + ChannelDelivery over the raw Gateway WS (websockets) + REST (httpx), no vendor SDK anywhere (tests incl.), so the manifest declares no pythonDependencies; imports core ONLY via personalclaw.sdk.*. gateway.py: full WS lifecycle — HELLO-driven heartbeat with ACK tracking, IDENTIFY with the intents bitfield summed from NAMED bits (guilds|guild_messages|direct_messages|message_content = 37377, pinned 3 ways + a dedicated DIRECT_MESSAGES guard, since dropping bit 12 yields 33281 and a bot that silently never receives a DM), READY->session_id/resume_gateway_url, RESUME(op 6) with the last processed seq, INVALID_SESSION resumable-vs-not, RECONNECT(op 7); the ZOMBIE trap is contained — a beat unacked when the next is due closes 4000 (never 1000, which makes the session unresumable) and resumes, and the sequence advances BEFORE dispatch so a raising handler cannot replay one event forever. api.py: PER-BUCKET rate limiting (Discord's real difference from a flat retry_after) — bucket state folded from X-RateLimit-Bucket/Remaining/Reset-After, an exhausted bucket waited off PRE-EMPTIVELY instead of spending a 429, a GLOBAL limit tracked separately from a per-route one, buckets keyed on method+concrete path so one busy channel cannot stall another, pathological retry_after capped, 'Authorization: Bot <token>' prefix pinned by test. delivery.py: approvals as message COMPONENTS (Approve/Deny action row, request id in custom_id, the INTERACTION_CREATE press always acknowledged inside Discord's 3s window even for a stale id, then the prompt edited to its outcome with components=[] so no clickable Approve survives), throttled edit-streaming with an exact final flush, 2000-char splitting, redaction on every send, real guild+DM thread links. transport.py: the REAL core trust seam (guard_inbound, provider 'discord') with is_dm derived from the ABSENCE of guild_id (Discord's actual signal) and self-authored/other-bot messages dropped — MESSAGE_CREATE fires for the bot's own sends, a trap Telegram's getUpdates does not have. Honest capabilities: every True has an implementation (reactions->add_reaction, typing_indicator->show_typing, edits->streaming PATCH, attachments->multipart upload, threads->a thread IS a channel id), max_text_len=2000. settings.py + cli_setup/doctor: app-owned dm_activation + application_id (deliberately NOT a credential — Discord prints it publicly and it rides in every invite URL) in the app's own store; bot token in the shared credential store under the app's own DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN key; setup prints the OAuth2 invite URL with exactly the 6 permission bits the code exercises (274878008384, no ADMINISTRATOR bit, test-guarded); doctor points at the Channels-page Test for the live GET /gateway/bot hello probe. Gate GREEN: manifest round-trip stable + validate() clean, SDK-only boundary lint clean (CI's repo-wide logic, conftest.py included), `python -m pytest discord-channel -q` -> 198 passed with no network and no wall-clock sleeps (httpx.MockTransport, a scripted fake WS, injected heartbeat/throttle clocks; trust exercised against the real seam in an isolated PERSONALCLAW_HOME), telegram-channel 108 still green. The zombie check, the 4000-not-1000 close code, the DIRECT_MESSAGES bit, the is_dm derivation, the self-message filter and the global-429 gate were each FALSIFIED by breaking them (each reds a specific test). Two defects the tests surfaced and fixed: _handle_dispatch coerced a bogus non-dict payload to {} and handed handlers a silently-empty event; and a tmp PERSONALCLAW_HOME alone is NOT isolation because core's save_credential mirrors into os.environ and load_credentials reads it back, so one test's owner id stayed visible to the next. Pre-existing, not from this change: slack-channel's TestCronMessageSplitting has 4 failures on a clean origin/main tree (verified by stashing the bundle out). Owner V4 (real Developer-Portal application + the MESSAGE CONTENT privileged intent + a bot invite to a test server, plan 'Owner tasks' 3) is a real-world owner step, pending outside this automated tick.

atoms.title: Email channel app (stdlib IMAP/SMTP in thread executors): poll transport+address-allowlist pairing, SMTP delivery+Message-ID threading, setup/doctor
atoms.scope: Session 6 — Email: T6.1–T6.3 + V6; Design §S6; Contracts C3 (Email column, streaming MUST-NOT)
atoms.done_when: fake-IMAP tests: new-mail detection, UID persistence, code-in-reply pairing; fake-SMTP tests: correct In-Reply-To/References headers and thread continuity across three messages via session_map; capabilities declare streaming=false; setup/doctor (IMAP/SMTP hosts + app-password guidance, probe=login+select) configure end to end; V6 real-mailbox validation recorded, digest-target deferral noted if plan-42 S5 absent (owner task 4: dedicated mailbox + app password)
atoms.evidence: PersonalClawApps/email-channel/ — a two-way conversational email CHANNEL (ChannelTransportProvider inbound + ChannelDelivery outbound) over stdlib imaplib/smtplib ONLY: no vendor SDK, no new pythonDependencies, core imported exclusively via personalclaw.sdk.*. Distinct from the sibling mail-inbox app (EIAT-2), which is a MessageSourceProvider with its own allowlist — per the plan boundary (EMAIL-INBOX-AND-TRIGGERS line 64) the channel REUSES the trust seam rather than forking one, so trust is owned by core channel_trust (provider="email") and this app keeps no allowlist. Both stdlib APIs block, so every IMAP/SMTP call crosses a thread executor — one blocking select() on the loop would stall the whole gateway. The poll loop is UID-based (never sequence numbers, which renumber on expunge and would silently skip or reprocess), read-only, and persists last_uid+UIDVALIDITY in the app's data dir so a restart neither reprocesses nor skips; the UIDVALIDITY check runs BEFORE the search and re-derives the cursor under the new numbering, so a renumbered mailbox RECOVERS rather than staying permanently skipped, and the advance lands before dispatch (and on CancelledError) so a raising handler cannot replay one message forever. Trust is keyed on the parseaddr address ONLY, with the local@domain shape verified rather than assumed (parseaddr hands back a bare token like 'not-an-address' as the address half — measured), so From: "bob@allowed.example" <attacker@evil.example> is denied; the display name is attacker-controlled and is used for UI text only. Self-authored inbound is dropped (providers copy sent mail into the inbox and a reply-to-self loops — the same trap Discord has via MESSAGE_CREATE). Unknown senders get one canned pairing reply and a later reply containing the 8-digit code redeems it via redeem_pairing_code; allowed non-owner content enters the session as guard_inbound's fenced_text, never raw; an unparseable message, missing From, or trust-store read failure denies and continues the loop (fail-closed). Outbound sets In-Reply-To plus an accumulating References chain keyed through session_map, so three messages stay one conversation. Per Contract C3 (Email column): deliver_text MUST, deliver_rich MAY as an HTML alternative, request_approval by reply token, upload_attachment as a MIME part, build_thread_link as a mid: anchor — and the streaming trio is MUST-NOT: ChannelCapabilities has no streaming field, so streaming-falsity is declared as edits=False (in every other channel a stream IS a repeatedly-edited message) with start_stream returning "" and no-op append/stop, both halves pinned by one test so the declaration cannot drift from the behavior. Gate GREEN: `pytest email-channel` -> 306 passed with no network, no wall-clock sleeps and no writes outside a tmp home (fake IMAP/SMTP servers and clocks injected, not monkeypatched onto stdlib); telegram-channel 108 and mail-inbox 32 unchanged; manifest round-trip through core's own AppManifest.from_dict -> 44 manifests valid + stable, validate() empty, permissions {storage, network}, no pythonDependencies; CI's ast boundary lint (which also covers conftest.py/_fakes.py) clean over 88 files, 11 of them this bundle's; flake8 --max-line-length=100 shows only the 9 E402s inherent to the app-loader sys.path prelude every bundle uses, zero E501. Six load-bearing controls were FALSIFIED by breaking them and restored: the UID advance/persistence, the self-message filter, the parseaddr-only trust match, the References chain across three messages, the streaming-trio no-op, and the fenced-text-into-session path (the parseaddr and cursor falsifications were re-run independently at tick level — each reds 4-9 specific tests). Three real defects surfaced by that falsification and fixed here: parseaddr accepting a non-address token as the trust key; the UIDVALIDITY check running AFTER the search (the exact failure it claimed to prevent); and imap_use_ssl declared in the settings schema with no setup writer, making a plain-IMAP port-143 mailbox unreachable from the CLI — an audit now shows all 12 declared keys have both a runtime reader and a setup writer. DEVIATIONS: the plan names EMAIL_IMAP_{HOST,USER,PASS,PORT}, but only the two *_PASS keys are secret, so only those live in the credential store (verbatim names) while hosts/users/ports live in ProviderSettings where the user can see and edit them, and no secret appears in settingsSchema at all (following mail-inbox). DEFERRED with reasons in the README: OAuth2/XOAUTH2 (DISCOVERY note; app-password auth documented for Gmail/Fastmail, which is what the plan specifies), IMAP IDLE (imaplib has no IDLE support — it means hand-rolling the command plus its 29-minute re-issue cycle; the 60s poll cadence is configurable), and the plan-42 S5 digest target (deliver_notification is the hook, but core notification_rules.TARGETS has channel_dm with no dispatcher wired, so a digest lands as an inbox item today; nothing in this app changes when it lands). Pre-existing and NOT from this change: slack-channel's TestCronMessageSplitting has 4 failures on a clean origin/main tree. Owner V6 (dedicated mailbox + app password, then a real send/receive/pairing walkthrough — plan 'Owner tasks' 4) is a real-world owner step, pending outside this automated tick.

Driven live on an isolated home: browser tab reads {connected:false, capabilities:{}} and the panel says 'Desktop app not connected'; register/push/unregister/stale-token round-trip and the 403s verified with the SEL trail (no credential in any row). REMAINING: (1) V2's on-device walk-through — Electron was never launched here, so the real TCC prompt path and the once-only prompt property are proven only by the state-machine unit tests, not on a device; (2) owner task 2 must approve the consent copy in the panel + Store bullet. DEVIATION: T2.4's 'fixture app can fire a native notification' is enforced at the gateway-mediated capability READ (GET /api/desktop/capabilities/{cap}); no bridge-backed USE route exists until DC-3/DC-5 build one, so the gate ships ahead of its first call site by design. Shipped in PR #1258.

atoms.done_when: global-hotkey push-to-talk (bridge global_hotkey cap, chord configurable in Settings) captures only while held/toggled with an always-on capturing indicator; renderer getUserMedia (TCC via bridge grant) chunk-uploads to existing /api/stt/transcribe and a spoken sentence lands in the composer at cursor <=2s after release on faster-whisper local; system-audio probe returns unavailable with reason and docs/guides/desktop.md states mic-only; deny-mic path degrades with an actionable prompt and an already-registered-chord conflict surfaces cleanly. (Owner tasks 3/4: mic-privacy sanity pass + default chord.)
atoms.status_note: PARTIAL (2026-08-16) — T3.1/T3.2/T3.3 implemented and gated; stays `todo` for V3. The renderer half is driven end to end in tests (chord push -> grant -> capture -> chunked upload -> insert at cursor, and every track stopped on release). THREE LEGS ARE UNEXERCISED because they need a launched shell on a real Mac: (1) that macOS delivers the global chord at all (globalShortcut is stubbed; Electron was never launched), (2) the real TCC prompt, (3) a real microphone (jsdom has neither getUserMedia nor MediaRecorder, so both are fakes). Also outstanding: owner task 3 (mic-privacy sanity pass) and owner task 4 (approve the default chord). DEVIATION: the global chord TOGGLES rather than reading key-release -- Electron exposes no global key-up event, so "held" is unreachable without an accessibility-class input tap we deliberately do not request; the done_when allows "held/toggled" and a 2-minute capture ceiling bounds a forgotten toggle.

atoms.evidence: docs/roadmap/research/windows-native-audit.md written as audit-only (zero implementation code, soul guardrail honored). Grounds every mechanism in verified as-built citations: process reaping via start_new_session/os.killpg (acp/transport.py:366/:456, escaped-child PPID walk :109-208) → Job Objects vs taskkill/T; chmod 0o600 enforcement (llm/credentials.py:96/:288-297, _enforce_perms on mode&0o077) → icacls/ACL seam (silent NTFS leak is the load-bearing risk); symlink creation at frontend.py:71/:98 + resilience/fixes.py:137 → junction/copy fallback; PTY at terminal.py:4-12 POSIX imports + :273 pty.openpty → ConPTY/pywinpty vs disable; service dispatch service/common.py:63-74 (no Platform.WINDOWS) → Task Scheduler vs Windows Service; sandbox detect_backend sandbox.py:596-618 + _spawn_exec_shim.py:54-85 degradation → isolation=none posture. Costed roll-up (M+M+S+S+S–M+M), explicit NO-GO with 4-criterion demand-evidence gate (≥10 native-only issues, top-5 community theme, WSL2/Docker genuinely-cannot-serve specificity, owner ratification of §6 posture), and a rung-2.5 finding: the unguarded gateway.py:3471 import resource ImportErrors at boot on native Windows. No code touched.

atoms.title: Disclose appMessaging targets at install consent (the last mile APE-9 left open)
atoms.scope: Traced defect, not a task row. apps/manifest.py:313 claimed of permissions.appMessaging "This is the install-consent surface for who an app can talk to, shown in the Store via to_dict" — true on the server (to_dict emits it, catalog._manifest_consent carries it into the pre-install entry, GET /api/apps returns it) and false at the last mile: AppPermissionsWire (web/src/lib/api.ts) never declared the field and PermissionList never rendered it, so the browser received the targets and dropped them. Measured on the unchanged component with {cron: true, appMessaging: ["receiver", "mail-*"]}: the whole consent output was "Permissions the gateway enforces • Scheduled jobs" plus EI-12 D2's network advisory. Owned here rather than reopened as APE-9 because APE-9's done_when covers the broker only and every clause of it holds — enforcement is real (apps/messaging.py:167 → can_use_app_messaging, 403 + SEL on an undeclared pair); the manifest comment overreached. Discovered during EI-12 D2 and recorded in that plan's log as needing its own atom. NOT the same shape as D2: D2 made network an ADVISORY row because app egress cannot be confined, whereas appMessaging IS enforced and belongs in the enforced bullets beside Storage / Scheduled jobs / Run background agents, uncaveated. Only D2's treatment of silence carries over — declaring no target is stated, not left blank. D2's load-bearing Object.keys(permissions).length > 0 Store-panel guard is untouched.
atoms.done_when: the Store names the apps a declaring app may message, in both surfaces PermissionList serves, among the permissions the gateway ENFORCES; a trailing-* target renders as the name prefix it is (mirroring _matches_any — the grant covers every current and future app under the prefix) and a bare * as any installed app; declaring none is disclosed as messaging no app (deny-by-default) rather than left silent; AppPermissionsWire declares the field and a test pins the server leg end to end (the pre-install catalog payload AND GET /api/apps, not just the component in isolation), backed by a two-sided rail that the wire type declares exactly the keys Permissions.to_dict() can emit; apps/manifest.py's comment is true afterwards. No first-party app declares appMessaging, so the rendering cases are synthetic manifests — stated plainly rather than implied — DONE 2026-08-13 (backend 18956 passed / 0 failed — baseline 18953 + 3 new; web 1832 passed across 192 files + 5 new; tsc + build clean; validated live in an isolated home)

Proved with a local git source carrying one schema-valid row: index named app-registry.json lists 1 app, named registry.json lists 0. OWNER DECISION: rename scratch/registry/registry.json to app-registry.json (42 refs across 14 files, all in unpublished scratch/ plus 2 tests, zero runtime blast radius) or widen core (rejected 2026-08-18 -- changes listing for every source). atoms.blocked_reason: PARTIAL 2026-08-26 (personalclaw.dev#31, rebase-merged 3cc45c89) - the pages, the cards, the per-app pages, the README fetch and the rebuild-picks-up-changes clause are all shipped and railed. TWO clauses remain, and the first is a PREMISE CORRECTION worth reading before anyone re-picks this. (1) THE REGISTRY DOES NOT EXIST AT THE PINNED CORE RELEASE. scratch/registry/registry.json 404s at v0.1.3 (2026-07-30); the registry tier landed on core main on 2026-08-18 (24f3f5c9, ET-3) and there is no newer tag. Verified independently with `git cat-file -e v0.1.3:scratch/registry/registry.json`. Reading core main instead would publish UNRELEASED core state as released state, so absence is recorded as a state (availability: 'absent-at-pin') and the page says so; the loader renders THREE states a card count cannot distinguish - absent-at-pin, empty, listed. So done_when's V4 ('a merged registry PR appears on the site after rebuild') is unreachable until the pin moves to a release containing the registry. What IS proven instead: changing the input and rebuilding changes the output. (2) 'card data matches the Store consent surface' is unverified against a live Store; what is asserted is that every consent value renders byte-equal and order-equal to its registry field, so it cannot disagree with any other reader of the same field. SECURITY SHAPE, since this is a pre-install trust surface: only the exact string 'clean' gets tone 'pass'; an unrecognised verdict presents as BLOCKING, never reassuring; 'no scan on record' renders as a distinct dashed treatment; permissions render permissions_declared verbatim and order-preserved. Anti-vacuity is explicit because the production registry is empty - a generator over it renders a clean zero-card page and every test passes for the wrong reason - so validate-registry-render.mjs fails if a registry with readable listings renders zero cards. CLEARS WHEN: core cuts a release containing scratch/registry/registry.json AND a community registry PR merges; then re-point the pin and V4 is measurable.

plans.summary: Enforcement floors, trust seams, and gate ergonomics for the platform. It corrects an unsafe resource-ceiling delivery mechanism (deliver rlimits after exec via a stdlib shim instead of a fork-unsafe preexec_fn), closes the unauthenticated app-backend inbound trust boundary with a proxy HMAC signature, and adds config/inert-surface drift baselines, an offline fake-model E2E harness, ceiling-intersect-profile guardrail wiring, flake root-cause fixes, and docs/aggregate-gate legibility. Most atoms originate here or deliver a specific mechanism correction; cross-plan edges mark work that lands into a plan another owner holds.

atoms.title: Post-exec resource-ceiling shim + spawn tripwires
atoms.scope: Replace the unsafe preexec_fn ceiling-delivery mechanism (it forces a full fork() of the multi-threaded gateway and can wedge a child holding inherited fds like gateway.lock and the listening socket, blocking the event loop with no await point) with a stdlib-only exec shim prepended to argv that setrlimits in the already-exec'd single-threaded child then os.execv's the real target. Add ResourceCeilings plus four profiles: tool (default, full ceiling + oom_score_adj bias to prefer killing agent work), session_host (raises NOFILE to the inherited hard limit for ACP hosts multiplexing many MCP pipes, no OOM bias), build (keeps OOM bias), none (user terminal, no limits/no bias). Add spawn_shim_argv/create_subprocess_limited and wire sandbox.nofile/max_pids/max_rss_mb config 4-point (dataclass + _meta, load, to_dict, write path). Route all agent-influenced async seams (native bash, bash action provider, subagent, app backends, MCP stdio, ACP transport, loop gates/worktree) through the shim; terminal gets none; frontend/service/update spawns operator-exempt. Add two AST tripwires: every subprocess/Popen/run/StdioServerParameters site is in a ceiling-wrapped-or-operator-exempt allowlist, and no async spawn site passes preexec_fn (documented exceptions only). Audit the watchdog-thread backend respawn and the event-loop bash spawn for the pre-existing wedge form. This supersedes and rewrites the EXECUTION-ISOLATION EI-A1/EI-A2/EI-A3 mechanism, whose single-threaded-at-fork premise is false (67 thread-creation sites; backends respawn off a daemon thread).
atoms.done_when: A child reports the ceiling via ulimit -n; the shim imports and runs with no core dependency; config round-trips; ACP sessions still open with multiple MCP servers (no EMFILE regression); adding an unmapped Popen site or an async preexec_fn reds CI naming file:line; validated on the dev gateway (ulimit, bounded fork bomb contained, terminal open with no shim cost, watchdog-revived backend carries the ceiling); the two hazard-site audits either yield a wedge regression test or a recorded finding that they are safe.
atoms.evidence: _spawn_exec_shim.py post-exec setrlimit; ResourceCeilings 4 profiles; 8 seams routed; 2 AST tripwires; sandbox.* config 4-point

atoms.title: cgroup v2 second enforcement tier
atoms.scope: Add an opt-in sandbox.cgroup_scopes tier on Linux as a second enforcement layer above the NOFILE floor: systemd-run --user --scope with TasksMax, MemoryMax, and MemorySwapMax=0. Probe once for a unified cgroup hierarchy plus a systemd user session and add the probe line to the doctor. On macOS, non-systemd, or containers, emit exactly one loud warning naming what is not enforced (pids/RSS) while NOFILE still applies; the probe never raises.
atoms.done_when: On a Linux fixture a fork bomb hits pids.max and dies contained; on macOS one warning states pids/RSS are not enforced; the probe never raises under any environment.

atoms.title: App-backend inbound proxy-signature authentication
atoms.scope: Close the unauthenticated inbound half of the app-platform trust boundary. App backends bind loopback with no caller check, so any local process that finds the port talks to the backend directly, bypassing the gateway proxy, session auth, and the app permission middleware; loopback binding is a network boundary, not an authorization one. Mint a per-app proxy secret at install/first-boot (apps_dir/<app>/.app_secret, mode 0600) and hand it to the backend by env. Sign every proxied request in the app proxy: X-PersonalClaw-Proxy: <ts>:<hmac> over <ts>:<METHOD>:<path>[?query]:<sha256(body)>. Verify fail-closed in the SDK app-server helper (absent/malformed/stale beyond +-60s/wrong signature -> 401, no route body runs, constant-time compare, denials to SEL). Roll every first-party backend onto the verifying helper (cross-repo, core helper first then apps in the same session). Document honestly that loopback is not authorization and the signature is what makes the permission model hold; add a CHANGELOG entry. Secret mint is also fail-closed: a backend that cannot read its secret does not start rather than starting unprotected.
atoms.done_when: A direct curl to the backend port is refused; a signed request replayed after the window is refused; a valid proxied request succeeds; the secret file is 0600 and never logged; every first-party backend refuses unsigned requests and the full app-boot path runs green; the doc states what each layer does and does not buy.

Confirm the bash action provider's existing _scrub_env is the allowlist shape or align it. Reuses the allowlist shape already specified by EXECUTION-ISOLATION's D1; this only extends it to the sites D1 does not name.

atoms.scope: Build a deterministic scripted fake model provider fixture (scripted responses, tool-call emission, zero network) usable as a real bound provider, reusing the empty seed fixture path. Add make test-e2e that boots a real gateway on the fake provider with a seeded authenticated session then runs web/e2e/ — skipped unless PERSONALCLAW_E2E=1, forced serial with addopts cleared, its own high timeout, and no coverage instrumentation on the subprocess gateway. atoms.title: Ceiling-intersect-profile guardrail wiring
atoms.scope: Wire the SafetyProfile family, which shipped with zero non-test callers (a declared decision object nothing consults). Add a Ceiling loaded once at boot from an operator-owned path the agent process cannot weaken; resolve(ceiling, profile) returns the intersection under tightest-wins (the profile may only narrow). Implement four archetypes each with one compose function (ScopedRuleset, OrdinalControl, CapabilityGate, ScopedMap), dispatching on archetype not scope name so adding a scope is data, not engine code; matchers and ordinal scales live in enforcer-owned registries; an unknown matcher aborts governance boot fail-closed. Encode the path-matcher rule as table-driven tests: normalize only the queried item (expand ~ and $VAR, then abspath) and never run the pattern through normpath (normpath treats */** as ordinary segments and collapses an adjacent .. against them, e.g. /a/**/../b -> /a/b, silently dropping the ** and widening an allow or shrinking a deny); cover /a/**/../b, a .. traversal against an allow-prefix, and a relative item against an absolute deny. Wire profile_for_session into the three dispatch seams plus spawn so the guardrail success criterion holds in code, proven by driving a real unattended trigger rather than a constructed object; composes with PHF-1 (profile picks tools/egress, the sandbox ceilings pick blast radius). Owner decision required on the ceiling's trust-root path and how it is protected from the agent on a single-user machine; document what the layer does and does not buy.
atoms.done_when: A profile cannot widen the ceiling (test per archetype); an unknown matcher aborts boot with a WHAT/WHY/FIX error; a normpath-on-pattern implementation reds the matcher tests; a real unattended trigger resolves through the headless profile with a live reader; a narrower profile bites and a widening attempt is refused, confirmed from logs/SEL.

atoms.title: Suite flake root-cause fixes + xdist scheduler decision
atoms.scope: Fix two suite flakes at their root, then decide the parallel scheduler with measurements. Knowledge-merge flake: close the KnowledgeStore connection in fixture teardown (no rerun, no xfail) so the suite runs clean of unclosed-sqlite resource warnings. Subagent SEL flake: the SEL audit call sits inside a swallowing except Exception, so contention makes the patched mock never fire; narrow the except so a genuine audit-write failure surfaces instead of vanishing, and give the two tests an isolated home — a silently-swallowed SEL write is a security-audit gap, not a test problem. Only after the root causes are gone, decide the xdist scheduler last and with measurements: switch --dist worksteal to loadgroup only if the suite wall-time regression is acceptable, recording the before/after either way (the serialization group mark is the real deliverable, not the scheduler choice). Reconcile the two flake memories so a fixed flake is not left documented as pre-existing.
atoms.done_when: The full suite runs 5x consecutively with zero unclosed-database resource warnings and both named tests pass deterministically; a genuine SEL write failure now raises rather than skipping; the scheduler wall-time measurement is recorded and the decision made; both flake memories are updated or deleted.

atoms.title: Docs-lint + plan-hygiene gate
atoms.scope: Add scripts/docs_lint.py, make docs-lint, and a blocking CI job checking dead relative links, missing anchors, file.py:NNN citations whose file no longer exists, and code-fence language tags; ship at the measured population with a shrink-only allowlist rather than at zero. atoms.title: Aggregate gates report, they don't short-circuit
atoms.scope: Convert run_prepush.sh from a short-circuiting && chain into a runner: run every independent check, capture all output, print one result table, and exit non-zero if any failed, with the verdict computed from the collected data rather than inline. Do the same for the website's test:ci aggregate, respecting the repo-owned pre-push hook and never weakening an assertion to go green. An && chain of N independent checks reports only the first failure, so a tree with several unrelated problems costs multiple push/wait rounds to discover over independent measurements of the same commit.
atoms.done_when: A tree with three independent failures reports all three in one run; each aggregate prints one result table with every failure visible in a single run.

atoms.title: Teach the inert-surface census whole-enum iteration — the false-red class its own docstring promised was impossible
atoms.scope: Corrects PHF-6's census (scripts/generate_inert_surface_baseline.py), whose enum detector documented its own error direction as "never a false red" and then produced one. Whole-enum iteration reaches every member by construction, so one iteration site now clears every member of the iterated class; resolution is import-aware so one of the seven Verdict enums cannot clear another's members. The generator states the detected shapes, the honest trade (more under-reporting bought for the elimination of this false-red class), and the KNOWN remaining false-red shape. Baseline regenerated by the tool, every delta accounted for against the code. The shrink-only forbidden-to-raise ratchet is untouched.
atoms.done_when: whole-enum iteration clears every member of the iterated class, across for/async for, all four comprehension forms, and the list/tuple/set/frozenset/sorted/iter/reversed/enumerate family, matched bare (E) or module-qualified (mutations.OpKind) and resolved through the ITERATING file's own imports so one of the seven Verdict enums cannot clear another's members; the generator states the detected shapes, the honest trade, and value-lookup E(value) as the KNOWN remaining false-red shape; inert-surface-baseline.json regenerated BY THE TOOL (145 -> 140 total, enum 18 -> 13) with every departure verified reachable at a named iteration site and nothing entering; fixture-tree tests pin iteration-only NOT flagged, consumed-nowhere flagged, a same-named enum elsewhere NOT cleared, and a vacuity guard that the census still sees >50 enum classes and still reports members; the shrink-only ratchet is untouched and proven to still red on a real new inert member.
atoms.evidence: FINDING: the audit instrument violated the invariant it documents. _inert_enum_surfaces stated its rule and its error direction explicitly -- "An enum member whose name is never accessed as an attribute anywhere in src/ is declared and never referenced... Iteration-only consumption (for m in E:) is not detected; that is the accepted under-reporting direction (NEVER A FALSE RED)" -- and then produced exactly that false red. workflows/publish.py declares Lineage = SOURCE/INFORMED_BY/RELATED and parse_publish (publish.py:136) validates author-supplied edges against the whole enum BY ITERATION: `if edge not in {e.value for e in Lineage}` with the expectation list `{[e.value for e in Lineage]}` in the error string. A template author writes lineage: {informed_by: [...]}, it validates, flatten_lineage (publish.py:433) persists it as a lineage_informed_by scalar on the artifact event, and upsert_plan (publish.py:240-246) only adds the SOURCE run marker on top of whatever the spec declared. Both members reachable and functional; the baseline listed enum:Lineage.INFORMED_BY and enum:Lineage.RELATED as inert. WHY IT MATTERS: five recent atoms were picked off this baseline, so a false red sends an implementer to wire up code that already works, and the census's whole value is that a reported surface is really dead. SHAPES NOW DETECTED: for/async for over E; all four comprehension forms (set/list/dict/generator); and the whole-iterable builtins list/tuple/set/frozenset/sorted/iter/reversed/enumerate applied to E -- each matched bare (E) or module-qualified (mutations.OpKind at workflows/service.py:1748, detectors.Skip at learning/template_gate.py:119, grill_mod.Channel at mcp_workflows.py:1078, all three real shapes in this tree). DELIBERATELY NOT DETECTED, each staying on the under-reporting side: E.__members__/_member_map_ walks (zero occurrences measured), getattr(E, name), value-lookup construction E(value), `value in E` containment (zero occurrences measured), iteration over a local alias, and out-of-repo consumers. isinstance(x, E) was excluded after a first pass wrongly counted it as iteration. RESOLUTION IS IMPORT-AWARE, NOT NAME-BASED -- the landmine: src/ declares SEVEN distinct Verdict enums (learning/accountability.py, learning/proposals.py, supply_chain.py, triggers/disposition.py, triggers/screen.py, workflows/judge_contract.py, workflows/verify.py). workflows/verify.py:76 runs `for verdict in Verdict:` over ITS OWN Verdict; a name-only index would have cleared workflows/judge_contract.py's Verdict.REPLAN on the strength of an unrelated namesake and silently deleted a real finding. So each iterated name resolves through the iterating file's own bindings (local ClassDef, from x import E [as A] incl. relative levels, and module aliases), falling back to every same-named class only when resolution fails -- and that fallback lands on the under-reporting side, never on a false red. TRADE, STATED IN THE TOOL: clearing a whole class per iteration site buys the elimination of this false-red class with MORE under-reporting (a member with no producer goes unreported once anything iterates its class). Proven, not asserted: temporarily adding an unreferenced PHF12_UNDERREPORT_PROBE member to the iterated Lineage kept the suite at 15 passed -- it is NOT reported, which is the documented cost. Reverted by a targeted edit, never git checkout --. STANDING RULE now written in the generator: when a reported surface turns out to be reachable through an unrecognised shape, TEACH THE DETECTOR THE SHAPE -- never hand-edit the baseline, never relax forbidden-to-raise. DELTA, FULLY ACCOUNTED: 145 -> 140 total, enum 18 -> 13, sdk_export 127 unchanged, config/trigger_kind/editable_config 0 unchanged. FIVE surfaces LEFT, ZERO entered. (1-3) loop/loop.py enum:LoopKind.DESIGN, .GENERAL, .GOAL -- iteration site loop/loop.py:39 `KINDS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(k.value for k in LoopKind)`, and KINDS is a live validator: loop/store.py:26 imports it and store.py:279 refuses `if loop.kind not in KINDS`, so all three are author-supplied kind strings that validate. (4-5) workflows/publish.py enum:Lineage.INFORMED_BY, .RELATED -- iteration sites publish.py:136 (the validation set) and publish.py:137 (the error-message expectation list), persisted by flatten_lineage. Every departure has a named iteration site; nothing was hand-removed. DISCOVERY -- A SECOND, DISTINCT FALSE-RED CLASS REMAINS, deliberately not fixed here: value-lookup construction E(value) also makes every member reachable when the value is externally supplied. judge_contract.py:342 does `Verdict(str(raw.get("verdict", "")).upper())` on MODEL-EMITTED text, so REPLAN is reachable and still reported. Six of the thirteen surviving enum surfaces sit on classes constructed that way (memory_record.py:216/218 MemoryTier/MemoryScope, tasks/models.py:74 DependencyType, workflows/confirmation.py:177 Status, workflows/judge_actors.py:84 Actor, judge_contract.py:342 Verdict). Unlike iteration, E(value) does not prove reachability by itself -- a deserializer fed only from internally-written state proves nothing -- so separating author/model-supplied values from our own round-trip is a judgment call worth its own atom, not a widening of this one. Named in the detector docstring and LEFT IN THE BASELINE rather than blessed away. RATCHET UNTOUCHED AND PROVEN TO STILL BITE: temporarily adding Completeness.PHF12_RATCHET_PROBE to workflows/containers.py (a shipped, non-iterated enum) reds test_no_per_file_counter_rose_vs_committed_baseline naming the file and the surface ("containers.py: inert surfaces rose 1 -> 2; new declared-but-inert surface(s): ['enum:Completeness.PHF12_RATCHET_PROBE']") plus the byte-match test -- 2 failed, 13 passed; reverted by a targeted edit. TESTS (5 new, in tests/test_inert_surface_baseline.py, all against a FIXTURE tree or the real tree -- no dead code added to src/): iteration-only enums across all three shape families are NOT flagged; a consumed-nowhere enum IS flagged and a half-read class still reports only its unread member; a same-named enum in another fixture module is NOT cleared by its namesake's iteration (the Verdict landmine); the Lineage regression on the real tree (its iteration site is seen AND no Lineage member is reported, so deleting that validation correctly reds); and a vacuity guard that the census still sees >50 enum classes and still reports >=5 enum members, so an over-clearing bug cannot read as a suspiciously clean census. NO baseline hand-edit: regenerated with `python scripts/generate_inert_surface_baseline.py`. No CHANGELOG entry -- a repo audit tool and its committed baseline are not a user-visible surface; no runtime behaviour, API, config, or frontend changed.

atoms.title: Per-class provenance verdicts for the census's 13 surviving enum surfaces — and the ruling that value-lookup E(value) must NOT clear a member
atoms.scope: A CLASSIFICATION atom over PHF-12's census (scripts/generate_inert_surface_baseline.py): it makes the census's verdict on each of the 13 surviving enum surfaces correct and evidence-backed, and deliberately builds no missing writer. Every E(value) construction site behind those surfaces is traced to the origin of its VALUE and classified EXTERNALLY REACHABLE / INTERNAL ONLY / DEAD CALL SITE. The ruling is that E(value) proves reachability only when the construction executes in production AND its value crosses a trust/authoring boundary, which is not expressible as a cheap deterministic AST rule — so the census rule is NOT widened, the shrink-only ratchet is untouched, and the verdict table plus per-member reasons ARE the deliverable. Corrects PHF-12's stated premise that judge_contract.py:342 makes Verdict.REPLAN reachable.
atoms.done_when: every E(value) construction site behind the 13 surviving enum surfaces is classified EXTERNALLY REACHABLE / INTERNAL ONLY / DEAD CALL SITE with file:line evidence; the verdicts live in the detector that produces the flags and PHF-12's superseded premise is corrected there; the census rule is deliberately NOT widened, so the shrink-only ratchet is untouched and the regenerated baseline is byte-identical (140 total, enum 13); three tests pin the ruling (value-lookup alone does not clear a member; the audited dead call sites still have no production caller; the verdict vocabulary is present in the generator and PHF-12's claim is refused) and the pin is proven able to fail by a temporary widening probe (enum 13 -> 7, 3 failed) reverted by a targeted edit; every member still flagged carries a one-line reason it is genuinely unreachable, plus what closing it would take, in PLATFORM-HARDENING-FLOORS's execution log.
atoms.evidence: FINDING: PHF-12's named-but-unfixed second false-red class rested on a FALSE PREMISE, and the audit is what showed it. PHF-12 recorded that judge_contract.py:342 (`Verdict(str(raw.get("verdict", "")).upper())`) runs on model-emitted text and therefore makes Verdict.REPLAN reachable. That line lives inside validate_verdict, and NOTHING in src/ calls validate_verdict: engine.py:1510 deliberately RESTATES the aggregation rule rather than importing it, and only tests (tests/test_workflows_judge_contract.py, tests/test_workflows_loop_templates.py) import the function. Model output never reaches that constructor. Same shape for judge_actors.py:84 Actor(...) (reached only from resolve_transition, whose only callers are in tests/test_workflows_judge_pretier.py) and judge_contract.py:224 `enum_cls(str(value))` for Ratchet (inside the equally uncalled hints_from_dict, and loop-bound so an E(value) rule cannot even see it). RULE DERIVED: E(value) proves reachability only when BOTH hold - the construction EXECUTES in production, and its value crosses a trust/authoring boundary. SIX SITES, AUDITED: (1) tasks/models.py:74 DependencyType(raw_type) - EXTERNALLY REACHABLE: tasks/handlers.py:242 calls registry.create_task(**body) on `await request.json()`, tasks/native.py:246 coerces via _coerce_dependencies, TaskDependency.from_dict (models.py:74) looks the member up, so a POST /api/tasks client picks REQUIRED_FOR; the bulk endpoint (handlers.py:164) is a second path. THE ONE GENUINE FALSE RED. (2-3) memory_record.py:216/218 MemoryTier/MemoryScope - INTERNAL ONLY: __post_init__ coerces rows read by from_semantic_row/from_episodic_row (vector_memory.py:1124/1129/1161/1169) that to_row wrote; the vault mirror (memory_vault.render_record) is render-only with no parse-back; every writer in memory_service.py passes WORKING/EPISODIC/SEMANTIC and SESSION/AGENT/GLOBAL, so "segment"/"workspace" never round-trip in. (4) workflows/confirmation.py:177 Status - INTERNAL ONLY: from_dict reads what to_dict wrote, and that is only pending/expired (resolve() returns a Resolution and never stamps RESOLVED; on_expiry returns EXPIRED). (5) judge_actors.py:84 Actor and (6) judge_contract.py:342 Verdict + :224 Ratchet - DEAD CALL SITES per the finding above. DECISION: DO NOT WIDEN. A syntactic E(value) rule would clear six classes of which exactly ONE is reachable - measured, not guessed: a temporary widening probe took enum 13 -> 7 (clearing MemoryTier.SEGMENT, MemoryScope.WORKSPACE, DependencyType.REQUIRED_FOR, Status.RESOLVED, Actor.WORKER, Verdict.REPLAN) and left Ratchet.RELAXED flagged anyway, so the rule would be unsound AND inconsistent. A false CLEAR is worse than the over-report it replaces: it buries a genuine gap inside every internal deserializer, and it passes the shrink-only ratchet silently because the count goes DOWN. Proving "provably outside" needs interprocedural dataflow (four hops across three modules for the DependencyType case), which is not a cheap deterministic AST rule. THE 13-MEMBER VERDICT: 1 false red (DependencyType.REQUIRED_FOR, left reported rather than cleared by an unsound rule); ONE reachable only OUT OF REPO by an app author (PromptCache.AUTOMATIC via sdk/provider_helpers.py:65 BrandedProviderSpec.prompt_cache, threaded at :334 - the census's declared blind spot, same reason sdk_export is 127); and ELEVEN GENUINELY unreachable, each with a named reason plus what closing it would take in the plan log. DISCOVERIES (not fixed here - classification atom): llm/capabilities.py:63-64 claims apps declare BrandedProviderSpec.structured_output, but that field does NOT exist on the SDK spec (provider_helpers.py:48-65 carries prompt_cache only), so grounding.py:492's live reader of a graded structured-output mode can never see anything but NONE; mcp_memory.py:41-49 advertises scope global|workspace on memory_remember and dashboard/handlers/schedule.py:181 drops the value entirely (write_lesson(rule, category, negative)), which is why MemoryScope.WORKSPACE has no writer; workflows/models.py:153 SessionMode is referenced NOWHERE in src/ (both members dead - FRESH is masked only because judge_contract.py:170 Isolation.FRESH shares the attribute name), the clearest delete candidate. NOT WIDENED, SO PINNED INSTEAD (3 tests in tests/test_inert_surface_baseline.py, 18 passed): test_value_lookup_alone_does_not_clear_a_member (fixture tree: a member reachable only via E(row[...]) is STILL reported); test_the_audited_value_lookup_call_sites_have_no_production_caller (real tree: validate_verdict / hints_from_dict / resolve_transition still have no production caller - it reds when one is wired up, which is the moment to re-verdict the member); and test_the_value_lookup_ruling_is_recorded_in_the_generator (the verdict vocabulary is present and PHF-12's superseded claim is refused). PROBE, REVERTED BY A TARGETED EDIT: the temporary widening reds exactly 3 tests - the new pin plus the two baseline-freshness tests ("3 failed, 15 passed"). RATCHET UNTOUCHED: forbidden-to-raise intact, no counter rose, baseline regenerated BY THE TOOL and byte-identical (140 total; enum 13, sdk_export 127, config/trigger_kind/editable_config 0). No src/ behaviour changed, no web/ change, no CHANGELOG entry - a repo audit tool and its committed baseline are not a user-visible surface.

atoms.title: Decompose config/loader.py below the ceiling — restore the headroom every config field needs
atoms.scope: The floor that PHF-5's and PHF-8's own rails predicted and that has now arrived. config/loader.py is 5900 lines against the ABSOLUTE 6000-line SIZE_CEILING_LINES, and tests/test_structural_baseline.py::test_the_ceiling_leaves_the_biggest_file_room_for_ordinary_maintenance asserts ceiling - max_file_lines >= 100. Headroom is exactly 100, so ONE added line reds the gate — and that test's own docstring names this file and this exact scenario ('adding one boolean toggle would red CI and demand a 5,427-line split as its price'). The file was 5427 when that rail was written; it has since grown 473 lines and spent all of it. Because the config round-trip contract (dataclass + _meta, load(), to_dict(), a write path, a frontend control) touches loader.py on EVERY new field, the whole remaining roadmap is blocked from adding user-facing configuration. Extract cohesive per-domain config sections into sibling modules under src/personalclaw/config/ and update their importers, following the src/personalclaw/agents/native/decision_tool_defs.py precedent created for this same rail at the 2800-line watch band. Clean break: no re-export shim. NOT in scope: raising the ceiling, widening the watch band, or regenerating the structural baseline to make the red go away — each of those retires the rail instead of paying it.
atoms.done_when: config/loader.py is at most 5400 lines (>= 600 lines of ceiling headroom, i.e. room for several ordinary config fields rather than one) with the extracted sections living in sibling modules under src/personalclaw/config/ and every importer updated — no re-export shim, proven by a RUNTIME import sweep with a stated count, not by mypy (ignore_missing_imports=true cannot see a stranded first-party import); tests/test_structural_baseline.py green including test_the_ceiling_leaves_the_biggest_file_room_for_ordinary_maintenance and test_the_watch_band_is_not_sitting_on_a_cliff, with the ceiling and the watch band UNCHANGED and structural-baseline.json regenerated only for the moved-file rows; tests/test_config_roundtrip.py green and the committed config-schema baseline (PHF-5) shows ZERO schema drift, proving the split moved code without changing one observable config key; and a NEW config field is added end-to-end in the same change as the proof that headroom was really restored — LV-4's learning.identity_report_* field, wired through all four round-trip points plus its frontend control, which also closes LV-4's only unmet clause.

plans.summary: Product-experience improvements to PersonalClaw's own surfaces: progressive-disclosure empty states that seed (never replace) the expert create flows, an always-open App Store category/source rail with polished cards, onboarding import from other local agent tools, artifact folders, local artifact deploy served through PersonalClaw's own gateway, artifacts as an indexed knowledge source, an always-on-conventions viewer, and a first-party product-app suite. Every simplification is progressive disclosure with full power one click away, and artifact deploy is strictly local through the PersonalClaw gateway with no cloud provisioner.

atoms.title: Onboarding import engine (scanners + writers)
atoms.scope: New onboarding/import package. Define ScanResult/ImportItem/WriteOutcome types and a source registry, then implement pure, fixture-testable scanners for the two highest-value sources: Claude Code (~/.claude: instruction docs, .mcp.json, settings.json, skills/) and Codex (~/.codex: AGENTS.md, config), with env-var-then-default root resolution (additional sources are additive later, not a v1 bar). Implement per-category writers to PersonalClaw destinations (instructions -> instruction docs, memories -> memory store, mcp_servers -> MCP config, skills -> skills/imported/<source>/ via the install-scan, schedules -> triggers, settings -> a review-gated merge that never clobbers) with a four-value outcome vocabulary (imported/existing/conflict/rejected). Enforce security floors on every imported file: is_sensitive_path refusal + credential/exfiltration-URL redaction, secrets counted-and-skipped and never imported; fingerprint-idempotent (SHA over source\0category\0key) so re-import never duplicates.
atoms.done_when: A fixture ~/.claude yields instruction+mcp+skills items with secrets counted-and-skipped and re-scan idempotent; importing the fixture creates the memories, MCP entries, and skills/imported/claude_code/*, and a conflicting item reports 'conflict' rather than silently overwriting.

atoms.scope: Add an onboarding step that surfaces detected sources ('We found Claude Code / Codex on this machine - import?') with per-category checkboxes, counts, and a conflict review; skippable and idempotent on re-entry (already-imported items shown as 'existing'). Wire GET/POST /api/onboarding/import. Validate against a fake source seeded under the dev home: run onboarding, import, confirm memories/MCP/skills landed and a planted secret did not, and confirm the skip path and re-entry idempotence.
atoms.done_when: Fresh home with a fixture source shows the step; import completes without any secret appearing; re-entry shows already-imported items as 'existing'; skip path works; validation recorded.

Support list/query by folder with the present-vs-absent distinction (None=all, ''=unfiled, id=that folder) and routes (GET /api/artifacts?folder=<id>). Artifacts library UI: folder tree in the side rail, drag-to-file, create/rename/delete, and an unfiled bucket.

atoms.title: Artifacts as an indexed knowledge source
atoms.scope: Extend the existing knowledge source framework so content-bearing artifacts are mirrored into the Knowledge Library without being listed as knowledge items. Add one aggregate artifact:// source row (source_type 'artifact') with per-artifact item grouping (an artifact's items replaced on edit / removed on delete without touching the rest) and a knowledge.auto_ingest_artifacts config (default on) fully round-tripped (dataclass+_meta, load, to_dict, write path). Emit change events from the artifact store and add a single in-process change-listener -> ingest/replace on upsert, remove on delete, routing artifacts through the existing FileReader path via a kind->extension map (html->prose extraction, md/text/json->text; widget/svg excluded) with redaction on the way in. First-enable backfill tied to source-row creation (idempotent). Artifacts surface only in search results with a provenance badge, never as knowledge items.
